sentences.zh: 允禟

translations.literal: Yunsi.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi.

sentences.zh: 輔國公允䄉履懿親王允祹怡賢親王允祥

translations.literal: Fuguo Gong Yun'e; Luyi Prince Yuntao; Yixian Prince Yinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun'e of the second rank, Fuguo Gong; Prince Yuntao, Luyi; and Prince Yinxiang, Yixian.

sentences.zh: 恂勤郡王允禵愉恪郡王允潖果毅親王允禮

translations.literal: Xunqin Junwang Yinti; Yukuo Junwang Yunxu; Guoyi Prince Yinli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yinti, Xunqin Junwang; Prince Yunxu, Yukuo Junwang; and Prince Yinli, Guoyi.

sentences.zh: 果恭郡王弘適簡靖貝勒允禕慎靖郡王允禧

translations.literal: Guogong Junwang Hongshi; Jianjing Beile Yunyi; Shenjing Junwang Yunxi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hongshi, Guogong Junwang; Beile Yunyi, Jianjing; and Prince Yunxi, Shenjing Junwang.

sentences.zh: 質莊親王永瑢恭勤貝勒允祜郡王品級誠貝勒允祁

translations.literal: Zhizhuang Prince Yongrong; Gongqin Beile Yunhu; Junwang-rank Cheng Beile Yunqi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongrong, Zhizhuang; Beile Yunhu, Gongqin; and Beile Yunqi, Cheng, of junwang rank.

sentences.zh: 諴恪親王允祕

translations.literal: Xianke Prince Yunbi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yunbi, Xianke.

sentences.zh: 端親王弘暉和恭親王弘晝懷親王福惠

translations.literal: Duan Prince Honghui; Hegong Prince Hongzhou; Huai Prince Fuhui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Honghui, Duan; Prince Hongzhou, Hegong; and Prince Fuhui, Huai.

sentences.zh: 聖祖三十五子：孝誠仁皇后生承祜、理密親王允礽，孝恭仁皇后生第六子允祚、世宗、恂勤郡王允禵，敬敏皇貴妃章佳氏生怡賢親王允祥，溫僖貴妃鈕祜祿氏生貝子品級允䄉，順懿密妃王氏生愉恪郡王允潖、莊恪親王允祿、第十八子允祄，純裕勤妃陳氏生果毅親王允禮，惠妃納喇氏生承慶、貝子品級允禔，宜妃郭絡羅氏生恒溫親王允祺、第九子允禟、第十一子允禌，榮妃馬佳氏生承瑞、賽音察渾、長華、長生、誠隱郡王允祉，成妃戴佳氏生淳度，良妃衛氏生第八子允禩，定妃萬琉哈氏生履懿親王允祹，平妃赫舍里氏生允禨，通嬪納喇氏生萬黼、允禶，襄嬪高氏生第十九子允禝、簡靖貝勒允禕，謹嬪色赫圖氏生恭勤貝勒允祜，靜嬪石氏生郡王品級誠貝勒允祁，熙嬪陳氏生慎靖郡王允禧，穆嬪陳氏生諴恪親王允祕，貴人郭絡羅氏生允䄔，貴人陳氏生允禐。

translations.literal: The Holy Ancestor had thirty-five sons: Empress Xiaochengren bore Chenghu and Prince Limi Yunreng; Empress Xiaogongren bore the sixth son Yunzuo, the Shizong, and Prince Xunqin Yinti; Imperial Noble Consort Jingmin Zhangjia bore Prince Yixian Yinxiang; Imperial Consort Wenxi Niuhuru bore beizi-rank Yun'e; Imperial Consort Shunyi Wang bore Prince Yukuo Yunxu, Prince Zhuangke Yunlu, and the eighteenth son Yunxu; Imperial Consort Chunyu Chen bore Prince Guoyi Yinli; Consort Hui Nara bore Chengqing and beizi-rank Yunzhi; Consort Yi Guoluoluo bore Prince Hengwen Yunqi, the ninth son Yunsi, and the eleventh son Yunli; Consort Rong Majia bore Chengrui, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, and Prince Chengyin Yunzhi; Consort Cheng Dai bore Chundu; Consort Liang Wei bore the eighth son Yinsi; Consort Ding Wanliuha bore Prince Luyi Yuntao; Consort Ping Heseri bore Yunxi; Imperial Concubine Tong Nara bore Wanfu and Yun'e; Imperial Concubine Xiang Gao bore the nineteenth son Yunxu and Beile Yunyi Jianjing; Imperial Concubine Jin Sehetu bore Beile Yunhu Gongqin; Imperial Concubine Jing Shi bore junwang-rank Cheng Beile Yunqi; Imperial Concubine Xi Chen bore Prince Shenjing Yunxi; Imperial Concubine Mu Chen bore Prince Xianke Yunbi; Lady Guoluoluo bore Yun'e; Lady Chen bore Yunxu.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor had thirty-five sons. Empress Xiaochengren gave birth to Chenghu and Prince Yunreng, Limi; Empress Xiaogongren to the sixth son Yunzuo, the future Yongzheng Emperor, and Prince Yinti, Xunqin; Imperial Noble Consort Jingmin, née Zhangjia, to Prince Yinxiang, Yixian; Imperial Consort Wenxi, née Niuhuru, to Yun'e of beizi rank; Imperial Consort Shunyi, née Wang, to Princes Yunxu (Yukuo), Yunlu (Zhuangke), and the eighteenth son Yunxuan; Imperial Consort Chunyu, née Chen, to Prince Yinli, Guoyi; Consort Hui, née Nara, to Chengqing and Yunzhi of beizi rank; Consort Yi, née Guoluoluo, to Prince Yunqi (Hengwen), the ninth son Yunsi, and the eleventh son Yunli; Consort Rong, née Majia, to Chengrui, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, and Prince Yunzhi, Chengyin; Consort Cheng, née Dai, to Chundu; Consort Liang, née Wei, to the eighth son Yinsi; Consort Ding, née Wanliuha, to Prince Yuntao, Luyi; Consort Ping, née Heseri, to Yunxi; Imperial Concubine Tong, née Nara, to Wanfu and Yun'e; Imperial Concubine Xiang, née Gao, to the nineteenth son Yunxu and Beile Yunyi, Jianjing; Imperial Concubine Jin, née Sehetu, to Beile Yunhu, Gongqin; Imperial Concubine Jing, née Shi, to Beile Yunqi, Cheng, of junwang rank; Imperial Concubine Xi, née Chen, to Prince Yunxi, Shenjing; Imperial Concubine Mu, née Chen, to Prince Yunbi, Xianke; Lady Guoluoluo to Yun'e; and Lady Chen to Yunxu.

sentences.zh: 允祿出為承澤裕親王碩塞後，允祚、允禌、允祄、允禝皆殤，無封。

translations.literal: Yunlu was given out as heir to Prince Yu Shuo Sai of Chenze; Yunzuo, Yunli, Yunxuan, and Yunxu all died young and received no titles.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu was adopted as heir to Prince Yu Shuo Sai of the Chenze line; Yunzuo, Yunli, Yunxuan, and Yunxu all died in infancy and were never ennobled.

sentences.zh: 承瑞、承祜、承慶、賽音察渾、長華、長生、萬黼、允禶，允騕、允禨、允禐皆殤，不齒序。

translations.literal: Chengrui, Chenghu, Chengqing, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, Wanfu, Yun'e, Yunxu, Yunxi, and Yunxu all died young and were not counted in the succession order.
translations.idiomatic: Chengrui, Chenghu, Chengqing, Saiyinchahun, Changhua, Changsheng, Wanfu, Yun'e, and Yunxu, Yunxi, and Yunxu likewise died young and were not entered in the order of seniority among the sons.

sentences.zh: 固山貝子品級允禔，聖祖第一子。

translations.literal: Gushan beizi-rank Yunzhi was the Holy Ancestor's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhi, of gushan beizi rank, was the Kangxi Emperor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 上有巡幸，輒從。

translations.literal: Whenever the Emperor went on tour, he always followed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor traveled on inspection, he accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年，命副裕親王福全禦噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he was ordered to assist Prince Yu Fuquan in resisting Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 he was ordered to serve as deputy to Prince Yu Fuquan in operations against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 上以允禔聽讒，與福全不協，私自陳奏，慮在軍中僨事，召還京師。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Yunzhi listened to slander, was at odds with Fuquan, and made private memorials, feared trouble in the army and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor found that Yunzhi heeded slander, clashed with Fuquan, and sent private reports; fearing discord in the field, he recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，福全師還，命諸王大臣勘鞫。

translations.literal: Before long Fuquan's army returned, and the Emperor ordered princes and great ministers to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fuquan brought his troops home, and the Emperor ordered the princes and senior ministers to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 福全初欲發允禔在軍中過失，會有嚴旨，戒允禔不得與福全異同，福全乃引罪。

translations.literal: Fuquan at first wished to expose Yunzhi's faults in the army, but there came a stern edict warning Yunzhi not to differ from Fuquan; Fuquan then took the blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuquan had initially meant to bring forward Yunzhi's misconduct in camp, but a stern edict warned Yunzhi not to oppose Fuquan; Fuquan thereupon confessed guilt himself.

sentences.zh: 語在福全傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Fuquan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: This is related in the biography of Fuquan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上征噶爾丹，命與內大臣索額圖統先發八旗前鋒、漢軍火器營與四旗察哈爾及綠旗諸軍駐拖陵布喇克待上。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the Emperor on the campaign against Galdan and was ordered, with Grand Secretary Sonin, to command the advance Eight Banner vanguard, the Han Army firearms brigade, four Chahar banners, and the Green Standard forces, encamped at Tuolingbulake to await the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he joined the Emperor's expedition against Galdan and, together with Grand Secretary Sonin, was charged to lead the advance Eight Banner vanguard, the Han firearms corps, four Chahar banners, and the Green Standard troops, holding Tuolingbulake until the Emperor arrived.

sentences.zh: 西路大將軍費揚古軍後期，下軍中大臣議，亦遣官諮允禔。

translations.literal: The western-route commander-in-chief Fiyanggū's army was late; the Emperor ordered the army's senior ministers to deliberate and also sent an official to consult Yunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Commander-in-Chief Fiyanggū on the western route fell behind schedule, the Emperor referred the matter to the senior officers in camp and also sent an envoy to seek Yunzhi's counsel.

sentences.zh: 上遂進軍昭莫多。

translations.literal: The Emperor then advanced to Jao Modo.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then marched on to Jao Modo.

sentences.zh: 既捷，允禔留中拖陵犒軍，尋召還。

translations.literal: After the victory Yunzhi remained at Tuoling to reward the troops and was soon recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory Yunzhi stayed at Tuoling to distribute rewards to the army and was recalled not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，封直郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was created Prince of the First Rank, Zhi.

sentences.zh: 三十九年四月，上巡視永定河堤，鳩工疏濬，命允禔總之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year the Emperor inspected the Yongding River dikes, mobilized labor for dredging, and ordered Yunzhi to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year the Emperor inspected the Yongding River levees, organized labor for dredging, and put Yunzhi in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月，皇太子允礽既廢，允禔奏曰：「允礽所行卑汙，失人心。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, after the crown prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunzhi memorialized: 'Yinreng's conduct is base and vile and has lost him the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year, after Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yunzhi memorialized: 'Yinreng's conduct is base and shameful, and he has lost the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 術士張明德嘗相允禩必大貴。

translations.literal: The diviner Zhang Mingde once read Yinsi's features and said he was certain to attain great eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Zhang Mingde had once read Yinsi's physiognomy and declared that he was destined for the highest fortune.

sentences.zh: 如誅允礽，不必出皇父手。」

translations.literal: If Yinreng is to be executed, it need not be by the Imperial Father's own hand.'
translations.idiomatic: If Yinreng is to be put to death, it need not be by Your Majesty's own hand.'

sentences.zh: 上怒，詔斥允禔凶頑愚昧，並戒諸皇子勿縱屬下人生事。

translations.literal: The Emperor in anger issued an edict denouncing Yunzhi as vicious, obstinate, and stupid, and also warned all the princes not to let their subordinates stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage and issued an edict condemning Yunzhi as vicious, stubborn, and foolish, and warned all the princes not to let their retainers make trouble.

sentences.zh: 允禔用喇嘛巴漢格隆魘術魘廢太子，事發，上命監守。

translations.literal: Yunzhi had employed the Lama Ba Han Geleng in sorcery to bewitch and bring down the crown prince; when the affair came to light the Emperor ordered him placed under guard.
translations.idiomatic: It emerged that Yunzhi had used the Lama Ba Han Geleng to work sorcery against the deposed crown prince; the Emperor then ordered him placed under surveillance.

sentences.zh: 尋奪爵，幽於第。

translations.literal: Soon his title was stripped and he was confined in his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his princely rank was revoked and he was confined to his residence.

sentences.zh: 四月，上將巡塞外，諭：「允禔鎮魘皇太子及諸皇子，不念父母兄弟，事無顧忌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, as the Emperor was about to tour beyond the passes, he instructed: 'Yunzhi has used sorcery against the crown prince and the other princes, with no regard for parents or brothers and without scruple in his actions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, as the Emperor prepared to tour beyond the frontier passes, he declared: 'Yunzhi has employed sorcery against the crown prince and the other princes, heedless of parents and brothers and reckless in all he does.

sentences.zh: 萬一禍發，朕在塞外，三日後始聞，何由制止？」

translations.literal: If disaster should break out while I am beyond the passes, I would not hear of it until three days later—how could it be stopped?'
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune should erupt while I am abroad, I would not learn of it for three days—how then could it be checked?'

sentences.zh: 下諸王大臣議，於八旗遣護軍參領八、護軍校八、護軍八十，仍於允禔府中監守。

translations.literal: He ordered the princes and great ministers to deliberate, and from the Eight Banners dispatched eight guard company commanders, eight guard lieutenants, and eighty guards to continue surveillance in Yunzhi's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He referred the matter to the princes and senior ministers, who arranged for eight guard company commanders, eight guard lieutenants, and eighty guards from the Eight Banners to keep watch in Yunzhi's mansion.

sentences.zh: 上復遣貝勒延壽，貝子蘇努，公鄂飛，都統辛泰，護軍統領圖爾海、陳泰，並八旗章京十七人，更番監守，仍嚴諭疏忽當族誅。

translations.literal: The Emperor further sent Beile Yanshou, Beise Sunu, Duke Efei, Banner Commander Xintai, Guard Commanders Tuerhai and Chen Tai, and seventeen clerks from the Eight Banners to take turns at surveillance, sternly warning that negligence would bring extinction of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also dispatched Beile Yanshou, Beise Sunu, Duke Efei, Banner Commander Xintai, Guard Commanders Tuerhai and Chen Tai, and seventeen banner clerks to relieve one another on watch, with a stern warning that any lapse would be punished by the extermination of the negligent man's clan.

sentences.zh: 雍正十二年，卒，世宗命以固山貝子禮殯葬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yongzheng he died; the Shizong ordered him buried with the rites of a gushan beizi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Yongzheng, and the Yongzheng Emperor ordered his burial according to the rites of a gushan beizi.

sentences.zh: 子弘昉，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: His son Hongfang inherited as Defender of the State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongfang succeeded to the rank of Defender of the State.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子永揚，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: His son Yongyang inherited as Bulwark of the State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongyang succeeded as Bulwark of the State.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: He was convicted of an offense and stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of an offense and deprived of his rank.

sentences.zh: 高宗以允禔第十三子弘晌封奉恩將軍，世襲。

translations.literal: The Gaozong enfeoffed Yunzhi's thirteenth son Hongshang as General by Grace, with perpetual inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor enfeoffed Yunzhi's thirteenth son Hongshang as General by Grace, with hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 理密親王允礽，聖祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Limi Yinreng was the Holy Ancestor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yinreng, Limi, was the Kangxi Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年十二月乙丑，聖祖以太皇太后、皇太后命立為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Kangxi the Holy Ancestor, by order of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, established him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the twelfth month of Kangxi 14 the Kangxi Emperor, at the command of the Grand Empress Dowager and the Empress Dowager, invested him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子方幼，上親教之讀書。

translations.literal: The crown prince was still young; the Emperor personally taught him to read.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was still a child, and the Emperor himself taught him to read.

sentences.zh: 六歲就傅，令大學士張英、李光地為之師，又命大學士熊賜履授以性理諸書。

translations.literal: At six he received a tutor; the Emperor appointed Grand Secretaries Zhang Ying and Li Guangdi as his teachers and also ordered Grand Secretary Xiong Cili to instruct him in the Neo-Confucian classics.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he was given formal tutors: Grand Secretaries Zhang Ying and Li Guangdi were appointed his teachers, and Grand Secretary Xiong Cili was charged to instruct him in Neo-Confucian texts.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，上召江寧巡撫湯斌，以禮部尚書領詹事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Emperor summoned Jiangning Governor Tang Bin and appointed him Minister of Rites with concurrent charge as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Emperor recalled Jiangning Governor Tang Bin and appointed him Minister of Rites while entrusting him with the post of Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 斌薦起原任直隸大名道耿介為少詹事，輔導太子。

translations.literal: Bin recommended the former Zhili Daming Circuit Intendant Geng Jie to be appointed Junior Tutor to assist in guiding the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin recommended the former Zhili Daming circuit intendant Geng Jie for appointment as Junior Tutor to assist in the crown prince's education.

sentences.zh: 介旋以疾辭。

translations.literal: Jie soon resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jie soon resigned, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，斌亦卒。

translations.literal: The following year Bin also died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Tang Bin also died.

sentences.zh: 太子通滿、漢文字，嫻騎射，從上行幸，賡詠斐然。

translations.literal: The crown prince mastered Manchu and Chinese script, was skilled in horsemanship and archery, followed the Emperor on tours, and composed verse with notable elegance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince mastered both Manchu and Chinese writing, was accomplished in riding and archery, accompanied the Emperor on his travels, and composed poetry of evident grace.

sentences.zh: 二十九年七月，上親征噶爾丹，駐蹕古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山，遘疾，召太子及皇三子允祉至行宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year the Emperor personally campaigned against Galdan and halted at Mount Gurufurjianjia Hunga; taken ill, he summoned the crown prince and the third prince Yunzhi to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year the Emperor led the campaign against Galdan in person and halted at Gurufurjianjia Hunga Mountain; when he fell ill he summoned the crown prince and the third son, Prince Yunzhi, to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 太子侍疾無憂色，上不懌，遣太子先還。

translations.literal: The crown prince attended his illness without a look of concern; the Emperor was displeased and sent the crown prince back ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince attended him without showing distress, which displeased the Emperor, who sent him back ahead.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，禮部奏祭奉先殿儀注，太子拜褥置檻內，上諭尚書沙穆哈移設檻外，沙穆哈請旨記檔，上命奪沙穆哈官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year the Ministry of Rites memorialized on the rites for sacrifice at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors: the crown prince's kneeling cushion was placed inside the railing; the Emperor ordered Minister Shamoha to move it outside the railing; Shamoha asked that the order be recorded in the archives, and the Emperor stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year the Ministry of Rites reported on the rites for sacrifice at the Hall of Imperial Ancestors, noting that the crown prince's kneeling cushion had been placed inside the balustrade; the Emperor ordered Minister Shamoha to move it outside, and when Shamoha asked that the instruction be entered in the record, the Emperor dismissed him from office.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，冊石氏為太子妃。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Lady Shi was invested as crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year Lady Shi was invested as the crown prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 三十五年二月，上再親征噶爾丹，命太子代行郊祀禮；

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year the Emperor again campaigned against Galdan in person and ordered the crown prince to perform the suburban sacrifices in his stead;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year the Emperor again took the field against Galdan in person and ordered the crown prince to perform the suburban sacrifices on his behalf;

sentences.zh: 各部院奏章，聽太子處理；

translations.literal: memorials from all boards and courts were to be handled by the crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: memorials from all boards and courts were to be decided by the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 事重要，諸大臣議定，啟太子。

translations.literal: on important matters the great ministers were to deliberate and then report to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: on weighty matters the senior ministers were to deliberate first and then report to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 六月，上破噶爾丹，還，太子迎於諾海河朔，命太子先還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor defeated Galdan and returned; the crown prince met him north of the Nuo Hai River, and the Emperor ordered the crown prince to return ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Emperor routed Galdan and returned; the crown prince met him north of the Nuo Hai River, but the Emperor sent him back to the capital first.

sentences.zh: 上至京師，太子率群臣郊迎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached the capital the crown prince led the officials in suburban welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached Beijing the crown prince led the officials in the suburban welcome.

sentences.zh: 明年，上行兵寧夏，仍命太子居守。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor marched on Ningxia and again ordered the crown prince to remain as regent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Emperor marched on Ningxia and again left the crown prince to govern in his absence.

sentences.zh: 有為蜚語聞上者，謂太子暱比匪人，素行遂變。

translations.literal: Slander reached the Emperor saying the crown prince had grown intimate with worthless men and his former conduct had changed.
translations.idiomatic: Slander reached the Emperor alleging that the crown prince had taken up with unworthy companions and that his former conduct had altered.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，錄太子左右用事者置於法。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to the capital he arrested and punished those about the crown prince who wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Beijing the Emperor arrested and punished the crown prince's influential attendants.

sentences.zh: 自此眷愛漸替。

translations.literal: From this time his favor gradually waned.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Emperor's affection for him steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 四十七年八月，上行圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the forty-seventh year the Emperor went on the autumn hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the forty-seventh year the Emperor went on the autumn hunt.

sentences.zh: 皇十八子允祄疾作，留永安拜昂阿。

translations.literal: The eighteenth prince Yunxuan fell ill and was left at Yong'an Bayang'a.
translations.idiomatic: The eighteenth son, Prince Yunxuan, fell ill and was left at Yong'an Bayang'a.

sentences.zh: 上回鑾臨視，允祄病篤。

translations.literal: The Emperor turned back his carriage to visit him; Yunxuan's illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor turned back to see him, but Yunxuan's condition was critical.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「允祄病無濟，區區稚子，有何關係？

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: 'Yunxuan's illness cannot be cured; he is but a small child—what does it matter?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: 'Yunxuan's illness is beyond remedy; he is only a small child—what does it matter?

sentences.zh: 至於朕躬，上恐貽高年皇太后之憂，下則係天下臣民之望，宜割愛就道。」

translations.literal: As for myself, above I fear causing anxiety to the aged Grand Empress Dowager, and below I am bound to the hopes of all the realm's subjects; I ought to set aside personal feeling and resume the journey.'
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, I must not distress the Grand Empress Dowager in her great age, nor fail the expectations of the empire's subjects; I should set aside private grief and continue on my way.'

sentences.zh: 因啟蹕。

translations.literal: He thereupon resumed the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: With that he resumed the journey.

sentences.zh: 九月乙亥，次佈爾哈蘇台，召太子，集諸王大臣諭曰：「允礽不法祖德，不遵朕訓，暴戾淫亂，朕包容二十年矣。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the ninth month, halting at Bu'erhasutai, he summoned the crown prince and assembled the princes and great ministers, instructing: 'Yinreng does not follow the virtue of the ancestors or obey my teachings; he is violent, cruel, and dissolute. I have borne with him for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the ninth month, while encamped at Bu'erhasutai, he summoned the crown prince and assembled the princes and senior ministers, declaring: 'Yinreng has spurned the virtue of our forefathers and disobeyed my instruction; he is violent, cruel, and dissolute. I have tolerated this for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 乃其惡愈張，僇辱廷臣，專擅威權，鳩聚黨與，窺伺朕躬起居動作。

translations.literal: Yet his wickedness has grown ever more unrestrained: he insults and humiliates court ministers, monopolizes authority, gathers factions, and spies on my daily movements.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his wickedness has only grown: he insults and humiliates court ministers, arrogates power to himself, gathers factions, and watches my every movement.

sentences.zh: 平郡王訥爾素、貝勒海善、公普奇遭其毆撻，大臣官員亦罹其毒。

translations.literal: Prince Ping Niersu, Beile Haishan, and Duke Puqi have suffered his beatings, and great ministers and officials have likewise felt his malice.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ping Niersu, Beile Haishan, and Duke Puqi have been beaten by him, and senior ministers and officials have likewise suffered at his hands.

sentences.zh: 朕巡幸陝西、江南、浙江，未嘗一事擾民。

translations.literal: On my tours to Shaanxi, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang I never once disturbed the people.
translations.idiomatic: On my tours to Shaanxi, Jiangnan, and Zhejiang I never once imposed hardship on the people.

sentences.zh: 允礽與所屬恣行乖戾，無所不至，遣使邀截蒙古貢使，攘進御之馬，致蒙古俱不心服。

translations.literal: Yinreng and his followers have acted perversely without limit, sending agents to intercept Mongol tribute envoys and seizing horses presented to the throne, so that the Mongols are all disaffected.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng and his followers have behaved with unrestrained arrogance in every way, sending agents to intercept Mongol tribute missions and seizing horses presented to the throne, until the Mongols have lost all respect.

sentences.zh: 朕以其賦性奢侈，用凌普為內務府總管，以為允礽乳母之夫，便其徵索。

translations.literal: Because he is by nature extravagant, I appointed Ling Pu superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, thinking that as husband of Yinreng's wet nurse he would facilitate his exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his extravagant nature, I appointed Ling Pu superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, supposing that as husband of Yinreng's wet nurse he would facilitate his demands.

sentences.zh: 凌普更為貪婪，包衣下人無不怨憾。

translations.literal: Ling Pu proved even more greedy, and none of the bondservants under him were free of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Pu proved even greedier still, and every bondservant under him seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 皇十八子抱病，諸臣以朕年高，無不為朕憂，允礽乃親兄，絕無友愛之意。

translations.literal: The eighteenth prince lies ill; all the ministers, considering my advanced age, are anxious on my account, yet Yinreng, who is his elder brother, shows not the slightest brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: The eighteenth prince lies ill; every minister, mindful of my advanced age, is anxious on my account, yet Yinreng, his own elder brother, shows not a trace of brotherly feeling.

sentences.zh: 朕加以責讓，忿然發怒，每夜偪近布城，裂縫竊視。

translations.literal: When I reproved him he flared up in anger; each night he pressed close to the felt screen of my quarters and peered through the cracks.
translations.idiomatic: When I rebuked him he flew into a rage; night after night he pressed close to the felt screen around my quarters and peered through the cracks.

sentences.zh: 從前索額圖欲謀大事，朕知而誅之，今允礽欲為復仇。

translations.literal: Formerly Sonin plotted great matters and I discovered and executed him; now Yinreng seeks revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Sonin plotted treason and I discovered and executed him; now Yinreng seeks revenge.

sentences.zh: 朕不卜今日被鴆、明日遇害，晝夜戒慎不寧。

translations.literal: I cannot tell whether today I shall be poisoned or tomorrow murdered; day and night I am on guard and cannot rest easy.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot know whether I shall be poisoned today or murdered tomorrow; day and night I live in fear and cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 似此不孝不仁，太祖、太宗、世祖所締造，朕所治平之天下，斷不可付此人！」

translations.literal: One so unfilial and inhumane—the realm forged by the Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu and brought to peace under my rule—must on no account be entrusted to such a man!'
translations.idiomatic: A man so devoid of filial piety and humanity—the empire forged by Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu and brought to peace under my hand—must never be entrusted to such a person!'

sentences.zh: 上且諭且泣，至於僕地，即日執允礽，命直郡王允禔監之，誅索額圖二子格爾芬、阿爾吉善，及允礽左右二格、蘇爾特、哈什太、薩爾邦阿；

translations.literal: The Emperor spoke while weeping until he collapsed to the ground; that same day Yinreng was seized and Prince Zhi Yunzhi ordered to guard him; Ge'erfen and A'erjishan, the two sons of Sonin, were executed, along with Yinreng's attendants Erge, Su'erte, Hashitai, and Sa'erbang'a;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor spoke through his tears until he fell prostrate; that same day Yinreng was arrested and Prince Yunzhi, Zhi, was ordered to guard him; Ge'erfen and A'erjishan, the two sons of Sonin, were put to death, along with Yinreng's attendants Erge, Su'erte, Hashitai, and Sa'erbang'a;

sentences.zh: 其罪稍減者，遣戍盛京。

translations.literal: those whose crimes were somewhat lighter were banished to garrison duty at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: those whose offenses were judged less grave were banished to garrison duty at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 次日，上命宣諭諸臣及侍衛官兵，略謂：「允礽為太子，有所使令，眾敢不從，即其中豈無奔走逢迎之人？

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor ordered an announcement to the ministers and guard officers and troops, saying in substance: 'As crown prince Yinreng gave orders—who would have dared disobey? Surely among them there were those who rushed to curry favor?
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor ordered an address to the ministers and the guard officers and troops, saying in substance: 'As crown prince, Yinreng gave orders—who would have dared refuse? Surely some among you rushed to flatter him?

sentences.zh: 今事內干連應誅者已誅，應遣者已遣，餘不更推求，毋危懼。」

translations.literal: Now among those implicated the deserving of death have been executed and the deserving of banishment sent away; the rest will not be pursued further—do not be afraid.'
translations.idiomatic: Those implicated who deserved death have been executed and those who deserved banishment have been sent away; the rest will not be pursued—have no fear.'

sentences.zh: 上既廢太子，憤懣不已，六夕不安寢，召扈從諸臣涕泣言之，諸臣皆嗚咽。

translations.literal: After deposing the crown prince the Emperor's indignation would not subside; for six nights he could not sleep peacefully and summoned the accompanying ministers to speak through his tears; all the ministers sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: After deposing the crown prince the Emperor's anger would not ease; for six nights he slept fitfully and summoned the ministers in his train to speak through his tears, and all wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 既又諭諸臣，謂：「觀允礽行事，與人大不同，類狂易之疾，似有鬼物憑之者。」

translations.literal: He then again instructed the ministers, saying: 'Observing Yinreng's conduct, it is utterly unlike that of other men, resembling the disorder of mania, as though some demon possessed him.'
translations.idiomatic: He then told the ministers again: 'Judging by Yinreng's conduct, it is utterly unlike that of other men; it resembles mania, as though some evil spirit possessed him.'

sentences.zh: 及還京，設氈帷上駟院側，令允礽居焉，更命皇四子與允禔同守之。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital he set up a felt pavilion beside the Shangsi Yuan and had Yinreng dwell there, further ordering the fourth prince and Yunzhi jointly to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Beijing he pitched a felt pavilion beside the Shangsi Yuan and lodged Yinreng there, further ordering the fourth prince and Yunzhi to guard him together.

sentences.zh: 尋以廢太子詔宣示天下，上並親撰文告天​​地、太廟、社稷曰：「臣祗承丕緒，四十七年餘矣，於國計民生，夙夜兢業，無事不可質諸天地。

translations.literal: Soon an edict deposing the crown prince was proclaimed throughout the realm; the Emperor also personally composed a text reporting to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altar of Soil and Grain: 'Your servant reverently received the great succession more than forty-seven years ago; in state affairs and the people's livelihood I have labored day and night with diligence, and in nothing have I failed to make account before Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict deposing the crown prince was proclaimed throughout the empire; the Emperor also personally drafted a memorial reporting to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altar of Soil and Grain: 'Your servant has reverently borne the great succession for more than forty-seven years; in matters of state and the people's livelihood I have toiled day and night, and in nothing have I failed to answer before Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 稽古史冊，興亡雖非一轍，而得深懼祖宗垂貽之大業自臣而隳，故身雖不德，而親握朝綱，一切政務，不徇偏私，不謀群小，事無久稽，悉由獨斷，亦惟鞠躬盡瘁，死而後已，在位一日，勤求治理，斷不敢少懈。

translations.literal: Examining the ancient histories, rise and fall have not followed a single pattern, yet I have deeply feared that the great enterprise bequeathed by the ancestors might be ruined through me; therefore though personally without virtue I have myself held the reins of government; in all affairs of state I have not indulged partiality, not plotted with petty men, allowed nothing to linger long unresolved, and decided all by my sole judgment, striving only to exhaust my strength until death, and while I hold the throne for a single day to labor diligently for good government, never daring to slacken in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The histories show that dynasties rise and fall by many paths, yet I have deeply feared that the great enterprise our ancestors bequeathed might perish through my hand; though lacking in personal virtue I have held the reins of government myself, in all affairs refusing partiality, refusing collusion with petty men, allowing nothing to linger unresolved, and deciding all by my sole judgment, striving only to exhaust myself unto death; while I hold the throne for a single day I labor for good government and dare not slacken in the least.

sentences.zh: 不知臣有何辜，生子如允礽者，不孝不義，暴虐慆淫，若非鬼物憑附，狂易成疾，有血氣者豈忍為之？

translations.literal: I know not what guilt your servant has committed to bear a son like Yinreng—unfilial and unjust, violent, cruel, and dissolute; unless some demon possessed him and mania became his illness, what man of flesh and blood could bear to act thus?
translations.idiomatic: I know not what offense I have committed to father a son like Yinreng—unfilial and unjust, violent, cruel, and dissolute; unless some evil spirit possessed him and drove him to madness, what man of flesh and blood could bear to act so?

sentences.zh: 允礽口不道忠信之言，身不履德義之行，咎戾多端，難以承祀，用是昭告昊天上帝，特行廢斥，勿致貽憂邦國，痛毒蒼生。

translations.literal: Yinreng's mouth speaks no words of loyalty and faith, his person follows no conduct of virtue and righteousness; his crimes and perversities are manifold and he cannot inherit the sacrifices; therefore I proclaim this to August Heaven and the Supreme Lord and specially carry out his deposition, lest he bring grief to the state and torment to the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's lips utter no loyal or faithful word, his person follows no path of virtue or righteousness; his offenses are manifold and he cannot inherit the sacrifices; therefore I proclaim this to August Heaven and the Supreme Lord and hereby depose him, lest he bring sorrow to the state and suffering to the people.

sentences.zh: 抑臣更有哀籥者，臣自幼而孤，未得親承父母之訓子，遠不及臣，如大清歷數綿長，延臣壽命，臣當益加勤勉，謹保終始；

translations.literal: Moreover your servant has yet greater sorrow: from childhood I was orphaned and did not personally receive my parents' instruction in sonship, far inferior to your servant; if the Qing dynasty's mandate is long and my life is prolonged, your servant ought to redouble diligence and guard the beginning and end;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I have yet greater sorrow: orphaned in childhood, I never received my parents' instruction in how to be a son, and am far less worthy than they; if the Qing mandate is long and my years are extended, I ought to redouble my diligence and keep faith to the end;

sentences.zh: 如我國家無福，即殃及臣躬，以全臣令名。

translations.literal: if our state lacks fortune, let calamity fall on your servant's person alone, to preserve your servant's fair name.
translations.idiomatic: if our house lacks fortune, let the calamity fall on me alone, that my good name may be preserved.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝痛切，謹告。」

translations.literal: Your servant, overcome with anguish, respectfully reports.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, overcome with grief, respectfully reports.'

sentences.zh: 太子既廢，上諭：「諸皇子中如有謀為皇太子者，即國之賊，法所不宥。」

translations.literal: After the crown prince was deposed the Emperor instructed: 'Among the princes, whoever plots to become crown prince is a traitor to the state and shall not be pardoned by law.'
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was deposed the Emperor declared: 'Among the princes, whoever plots to become crown prince is an enemy of the state and shall not be spared by law.'

sentences.zh: 諸皇子中皇八子允禩謀最力，上知之，命執付議政大臣議罪，削貝勒。

translations.literal: Among the princes the eighth son Yinsi plotted most vigorously; the Emperor knew it and ordered him seized and handed to the Deliberative Princes for judgment, stripping him of his beile rank.
translations.idiomatic: Among the princes the eighth son Yinsi had schemed most actively; when the Emperor learned of it he ordered him arrested and referred to the Deliberative Princes for judgment, stripping him of his beile rank.

sentences.zh: 十月，皇三子允祉發喇嘛巴漢格隆，為皇長子允禔厭允礽事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the third prince Yunzhi exposed the Lama Ba Han Geleng in the affair by which the eldest prince Yunzhi had used sorcery against Yinreng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the third son, Prince Yunzhi, exposed the Lama Ba Han Geleng in the affair by which the eldest prince Yunzhi had worked sorcery against Yinreng.

sentences.zh: 上令侍衛發允礽所居，得厭勝物十餘事。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered guards to search Yinreng's residence and more than ten sorcery objects were found.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered guards to search Yinreng's quarters and found more than ten objects used for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 上幸南苑行圍，遘疾，還宮，召允礽入見，使居咸安宮。

translations.literal: The Emperor went to the Southern Park for the hunt, fell ill, returned to the palace, summoned Yinreng for an audience, and had him lodged in the Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went to the Southern Park for the autumn hunt, fell ill, returned to the palace, summoned Yinreng for an audience, and lodged him in the Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 上逾諸近臣曰：「朕召見允礽，詢問前事，竟有全不知者，是其諸惡皆被魘魅而然。

translations.literal: The Emperor addressed the close ministers, saying: "I summoned Yinreng for an audience, questioned him about earlier affairs, and there were matters of which he knew nothing at all—it was that all his evils came from being bewitched by sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: Addressing his close ministers, the Emperor said: "When I summoned Yinreng and questioned him about past events, he knew nothing of some things at all; all his wickedness was the work of sorcery bewitching him.

sentences.zh: 果蒙天佑，狂疾頓除，改而為善，朕自有裁奪。」

translations.literal: If indeed blessed by Heaven's aid, his mad illness is suddenly removed and he changes to do good, I myself will have judgment and disposal."
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven has indeed favored him, his madness vanishes at once and he turns to do right, I shall decide his fate myself."

sentences.zh: 廷臣希旨有請復立允礽為太子者，上不許。

translations.literal: Court ministers who sought to follow his intent requested that Yinreng be re-established as crown prince; the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Some court officials, eager to please, petitioned for Yinreng's reinstatement as crown prince, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 左副都御史勞之辨奏上，上斥其奸詭，奪官，予杖。

translations.literal: Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Lao Zhibian memorialized to the Emperor; the Emperor denounced him as treacherous and devious, stripped his office, and subjected him to bamboo beating.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Lao Zhibian presented a memorial, which the Emperor denounced as devious and slanderous; he was dismissed from office and beaten with the bamboo.

sentences.zh: 既，上召諸大臣，命於諸皇子中舉孰可繼立為太子者，諸大臣舉允禩。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor summoned the great ministers and ordered them to nominate from among the princes who could succeed as crown prince; the great ministers nominated Yinsi.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the Emperor summoned the senior ministers and asked them to name which prince might succeed as crown prince; they nominated Yinsi.

sentences.zh: 明日，上召諸大臣入見，諭以太子因魘魅失本性狀。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor summoned the great ministers for audience and instructed them regarding the crown prince's condition of losing his true nature through sorcery bewitchment.
translations.idiomatic: The following day the Emperor summoned the ministers and explained how the crown prince had lost his true nature through sorcery.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣奏：「上既灼知太子病源，治療就痊，請上頒旨宣示。」

translations.literal: The great ministers memorialized: "Since Your Majesty has clearly known the crown prince's source of illness and treatment has brought recovery, we request that Your Majesty issue an edict to proclaim it."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers submitted: "Your Majesty now understands the cause of the crown prince's illness and he has recovered; we ask that you issue an edict to announce this to the realm."

sentences.zh: 又明日，召允礽及諸大臣同入見，命釋之，且曰：「覽古史冊，太子既廢，常不得其死，人君靡不悔者。

translations.literal: The day after that, he summoned Yinreng and the great ministers together for audience, ordered his release, and said: "Perusing the ancient records, when a crown prince was deposed he often did not meet with a natural death, and no ruler failed to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Yinreng and the ministers together, ordered him released, and said: "In the history books, a deposed crown prince seldom died a natural death, and no emperor failed to rue the decision.

sentences.zh: 前執允礽，朕日日不釋於懷。

translations.literal: Formerly, having Yinreng in custody, I was never free of it in my heart day after day.
translations.idiomatic: While Yinreng was in custody, the burden weighed on my mind every single day.

sentences.zh: 自頃召見一次，胸中乃疏快一次。

translations.literal: Since recently each time I summoned him for audience, my breast became a little lighter once.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I have summoned him of late, my heart has felt a little lighter.

sentences.zh: 今事已明白，明日為始，朕當霍然矣。」

translations.literal: Now the matter is clear; starting from tomorrow, I shall suddenly be relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the matter is clear, from tomorrow onward I shall be wholly at ease."

sentences.zh: 又明日，諸大臣奏請復立允礽為太子，疏留中未下。

translations.literal: The day after that, the great ministers memorialized requesting Yinreng's re-establishment as crown prince; the memorial was kept at court and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day the ministers memorialized again for Yinreng's reinstatement as crown prince, but the memorial was held back and no response issued.

sentences.zh: 上疾漸愈，四十八年正月，諸大臣复疏請，上許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor's illness gradually recovered; in the first month of the forty-eighth year the great ministers again memorialized with a request, and the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: As the Emperor's health gradually improved, in the first month of Kangxi 48 the ministers petitioned again, and the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，復立允礽為皇太子，妃復為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day of the third month Yinreng was again established as crown prince, and his consort was again made crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the third month Yinreng was reinstated as crown prince, and his consort was restored as crown princess.

sentences.zh: 五十年十月，上察諸大臣為太子結黨會飲，譴責步軍統領託合齊，尚書耿額、齊世武，都統鄂繕、迓圖。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fiftieth year the Emperor investigated the great ministers' forming factions for the crown prince and feasting together; he rebuked Banner Commander of the Foot Tuheqi, Ministers Genge and Qi Shiwu, and Banner Commanders Eschan and Yatu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 50 the Emperor discovered that senior officials had been forming factions for the crown prince and holding convivial gatherings; he rebuked Banner Commander of the Foot Tuheqi, Ministers Genge and Qi Shiwu, and Banner Commanders Eschan and Yatu.

sentences.zh: 託合齊兼坐受戶部缺主沈天生賄罪，絞；

translations.literal: Tuheqi was additionally convicted for receiving bribes from Shen Tiansheng, chief clerk of a Ministry of Revenue vacancy, and was sentenced to strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: Tuheqi was also convicted of taking bribes from Shen Tiansheng, a chief clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, and sentenced to strangulation;

sentences.zh: 又以鎮國公景熙首告貪婪不法諸事，未決，死於獄，命剉屍焚之。

translations.literal: Also because Defender of the State Jingxi had been the first to report greedy and unlawful affairs, before the case was decided he died in prison; the Emperor ordered his corpse sliced and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxi, Defender of the State, who had been the first to expose greedy and unlawful conduct, died in prison before his case was resolved; the Emperor ordered his corpse dismembered and burned.

sentences.zh: 齊世武、耿額亦以得沈天生賄，絞死。

translations.literal: Qi Shiwu and Genge also for having received bribes from Shen Tiansheng were executed by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shiwu and Genge were likewise executed by strangulation for accepting bribes from Shen Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 鄂繕奪官，幽禁。

translations.literal: Eschan was stripped of office and placed in secret confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Eschan was dismissed from office and confined in secret.

sentences.zh: 迓圖入辛者庫，守安親王墓。

translations.literal: Yatu entered the Sinners' Ward and guarded Prince An's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yatu was sent to the Sinners' Ward to guard the tomb of Prince An.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「諸事皆因允礽。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed, saying: "All these affairs are because of Yinreng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor declared: "All these affairs arose from Yinreng.

sentences.zh: 允礽不仁不孝，徒以言語貨財囑此輩貪得諂媚之人，潛通消息，尤無恥之甚。」

translations.literal: Yinreng is unkind and unfilial; he merely used words and goods and wealth to instruct these grasping and fawning persons, secretly passing messages—most shameless of all.'
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng is unkind and unfilial; he merely used promises and bribes to enlist these greedy, fawning men, passing secret messages back and forth—the height of shamelessness.'

sentences.zh: 五十一年十月，复廢太子，禁錮咸安宮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifty-first year the crown prince was again deposed and confined at the Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 51 the crown prince was deposed again and imprisoned in the Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，趙申喬疏請立太子，上諭曰：「建儲大事，未可輕言。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year Zhao Shenqiao memorialized requesting the establishment of a crown prince; the Emperor instructed: "The great affair of establishing an heir is not to be spoken of lightly.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 Zhao Shenqiao petitioned for the naming of a crown prince; the Emperor replied: "The question of establishing an heir is too grave to be raised lightly.

sentences.zh: 允礽為太子時，服御俱用黃色，儀注上幾於朕，實開驕縱之門。

translations.literal: When Yinreng was crown prince, his attire and accoutrements were all in yellow, and his ceremonial protocol nearly equaled mine—it truly opened the door to arrogance and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinreng was crown prince, his dress and regalia were all yellow, and his ceremonial honors nearly matched my own—it opened the door to pride and license.

sentences.zh: 宋仁宗三十年未立太子，我太祖、太宗亦未豫立。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong of Song went thirty years without establishing a crown prince; our Taizu and Taizong likewise did not establish one in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Song Renzong went thirty years without naming an heir; our Taizu and Taizong likewise never designated one in advance.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐已事，太子幼衝，尚保無事；

translations.literal: In the precedents of Han and Tang, when the crown prince was young and tender, they still kept things uneventful;
translations.idiomatic: In Han and Tang history, when the heir was still young, the transition usually passed without incident;

sentences.zh: 若太子年長，左右群小結黨營私，鮮有能無過者。

translations.literal: But if the crown prince was grown in years, and petty men at his side formed factions for private gain, few could be without fault.
translations.idiomatic: But when the heir was grown and surrounded by petty schemers who formed factions for private gain, scarcely any escaped without fault.

sentences.zh: 太子為國本，朕豈不知？

translations.literal: That the crown prince is the foundation of the state—do I not know it?
translations.idiomatic: Do I not know that the crown prince is the foundation of the state?

sentences.zh: 立非其人，關係匪輕。

translations.literal: To establish one who is not the right person—the connection is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: To name the wrong man carries consequences too grave to treat lightly.

sentences.zh: 允礽儀表、學問、才技俱有可觀，而行事乖謬，不仁不孝，非狂易而何？

translations.literal: Yinreng's bearing, learning, and talents were all worth viewing, yet his conduct was perverse, unkind, and unfilial—if not mania and disorder, then what?
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's appearance, learning, and talents were all impressive, yet his conduct was perverse, unkind, and unfilial—what else could this be but madness?

sentences.zh: 凡人幼時猶可教訓，及長而誘於黨類，便各有所為，不復能拘制矣。

translations.literal: Ordinary men in youth can still be instructed and admonished; when grown and enticed by faction mates, each then has his own pursuits and can no longer be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: A man may still be taught in youth, but once he grows up and falls in with a faction, each pursues his own ends and can no longer be controlled.

sentences.zh: 立皇太子事，未可輕定。」

translations.literal: The matter of establishing a crown prince cannot be lightly decided."
translations.idiomatic: The question of naming a crown prince must not be settled hastily."

sentences.zh: 自是上意不欲更立太子，雖諭大學士、九卿等裁定太子儀仗，卒未用。

translations.literal: From then on the Emperor's intent was not to establish a crown prince again; although he instructed Grand Secretaries, the Nine Ministers, and others to settle the crown prince's ceremonial regalia, in the end it was not used.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Emperor had no wish to name another crown prince; although he once ordered the Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers to draft regulations for the heir's ceremonial guard, they were never adopted.

sentences.zh: 終清世不復立太子。

translations.literal: Through the end of the Qing dynasty a crown prince was never again established.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the rest of the Qing dynasty, no crown prince was ever named again.

sentences.zh: 五十四年十一月，有醫賀孟頫者，為允礽福金治疾，允礽以礬水作書相往來，复囑普奇舉為大將軍，事發，普奇等皆得罪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-fourth year there was a physician He Mengfu who treated illness for Yinreng's fujin; Yinreng used alum water to write letters back and forth, and again instructed Puqi to recommend him as grand general; when the affair came to light Puqi and others were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kangxi 54 the physician He Mengfu treated Yinreng's consort; Yinreng exchanged letters written in invisible alum ink and again asked Puqi to recommend him for appointment as grand general; when the plot was exposed, Puqi and the others were all punished.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，大學士王掞疏請建儲，越數日，御史陳嘉猷等八人疏繼上，上疑其結黨，疏留中不下。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Grand Secretary Wang Yan memorialized requesting establishment of an heir; after several days Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others memorialized in succession; the Emperor suspected faction forming and kept the memorial at court without issuing it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 56 Grand Secretary Wang Yan petitioned for the naming of an heir; a few days later eight censors led by Chen Jiayou submitted follow-up memorials; the Emperor suspected collusion and held the petitions without response.

sentences.zh: 五十七年二月，翰林院檢討朱天保請復立允礽為太子，上親召詰責，辭連其父侍郎朱都納，及都統銜齊世，副都統戴保、常賚，內閣學士金寶。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifty-seventh year Hanlin Academy proofreader Zhu Tianbao requested Yinreng's re-establishment as crown prince; the Emperor personally summoned and interrogated and rebuked him; his testimony implicated his father Vice Minister Zhu Duna, Banner Commander with rank Qi Shi, Vice Banner Commanders Dai Bao and Chang Ci, and Grand Secretary Jin Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kangxi 57 Hanlin proofreader Zhu Tianbao petitioned for Yinreng's reinstatement; the Emperor summoned him personally to interrogate and rebuke him; his testimony implicated his father Vice Minister Zhu Duna, Banner Commander Qi Shi, Vice Banner Commanders Dai Bao and Chang Ci, and Grand Secretary Jin Bao.

sentences.zh: 朱天保、戴保誅死，朱都納及常賚、金寶交步軍統領枷示，齊世交宗人府幽禁。

translations.literal: Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were executed; Zhu Duna together with Chang Ci and Jin Bao were handed to the Banner Commander of the Foot for cangue display; Qi Shi was handed to the Imperial Clan Court for secret confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tianbao and Dai Bao were put to death; Zhu Duna, Chang Ci, and Jin Bao were turned over to the Banner Commander of the Foot for public display in the cangue; Qi Shi was sent to the Imperial Clan Court for secret confinement.

sentences.zh: 七月，允礽福金石氏卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yinreng's fujin, Lady Shi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yinreng's consort, née Shi, died.

sentences.zh: 上稱其淑孝寬和，作配允礽，辛勤歷有年所，諭大學士等同翰林院撰文致祭。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised her as virtuous, filial, generous, and gentle; as consort to Yinreng she had labored diligently for many years; he instructed Grand Secretaries together with the Hanlin Academy to compose writings for offering sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised her as virtuous, filial, generous, and gentle, saying that as Yinreng's wife she had served diligently for many years; he ordered the Grand Secretaries and the Hanlin Academy to compose sacrificial texts.

sentences.zh: 六十年三月，上萬壽節，掞復申前請建儲。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixtieth year, on the Emperor's birthday celebration, Yan again renewed his earlier request to establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 60, on the Emperor's birthday, Wang Yan again pressed his earlier petition to name an heir.

sentences.zh: 越數日，御史陶彝等十二人疏繼上。

translations.literal: After several days Censors Tao Yi and eleven others memorialized in succession.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later twelve censors led by Tao Yi submitted follow-up memorials.

sentences.zh: 上乃嚴旨斥掞為奸，並以諸大臣請逮掞等治罪，上令掞及彝等發軍前委署額外章京。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued a stern edict denouncing Yan as treacherous, and since the great ministers requested arresting Yan and others for punishment, the Emperor ordered Yan and Yi and the others sent to the army front as acting extra clerks on detached duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued a stern edict denouncing Wang Yan as seditious; when senior officials requested that Yan and the others be arrested and punished, the Emperor instead ordered Yan, Tao Yi, and the rest dispatched to the front as acting supplemental clerks.

sentences.zh: 掞年老，其子奕清代行。

translations.literal: Yan was old in years; his son Yiqing went in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was elderly, so his son Yiqing went in his place.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，封允礽子弘晳為理郡王。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year the Shizong ascended the throne and enfeoffed Yinreng's son Hongxi as Prince of the Commandery of Li.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 61, when the Yongzheng Emperor ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Yinreng's son Hongxi as Prince of the Commandery of Li.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，詔於祁縣鄭家莊修蓋房屋，駐劄兵丁，將移允礽往居之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict ordered houses built at Zhengjiazhuang in Qi County, garrison soldiers stationed, and Yinreng to be moved to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 an edict ordered dwellings built at Zhengjiazhuang in Qi County, with a garrison of troops, and Yinreng was to be relocated there.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月，允礽病薨，追封諡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year Yinreng died of illness; posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yongzheng 2 Yinreng died of illness and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 六年，弘晳進封親王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hongxi was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 6 Hongxi was promoted to prince.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年十月，高宗諭責弘晳，自視為東宮嫡子，居心叵測，削爵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Qianlong the Gaozong instructed and rebuked Hongxi for regarding himself as the legitimate son of the Eastern Palace with unfathomable intent, and stripped his rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Qianlong 4 the Qianlong Emperor rebuked Hongxi for acting as though he were the legitimate heir of the Eastern Palace with motives that could not be fathomed, and stripped him of his title.

sentences.zh: 以允礽第十子弘㬙襲郡王。

translations.literal: Yinreng's tenth son Honghui inherited as Prince of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's tenth son Honghui succeeded to the commandery prince title.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he died; posthumous title Ke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-fifth year and was given the posthumous title Ke.

sentences.zh: 子永曖，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yongnuan inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongnuan succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants by precedent were reduced step by step, with Bulwark of the State perpetually inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants inherited in descending rank by precedent, eventually holding the title of Bulwark of the State in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 允礽第三子弘晉、第六子弘曣、第七子弘晁、第十二子弘晥皆封輔國公。

translations.literal: Yinreng's third son Hongjin, sixth son Hongyan, seventh son Hongchao, and twelfth son Hongwan were all enfeoffed as Bulwark of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Yinreng's third son Hongjin, sixth son Hongyan, seventh son Hongchao, and twelfth son Hongwan were all enfeoffed as Bulwarks of the State.

sentences.zh: 弘曣卒，諡恪僖。

translations.literal: Hongyan died; posthumous title Kexi was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyan died and was given the posthumous title Kexi.

sentences.zh: 子永瑋，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yongwei inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongwei succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 事高宗，歷官左宗正，廣州、黑龍江、盛京將軍。

translations.literal: Serving the Gaozong, he held posts as Left Director of the Imperial Clan, and General at Guangzhou, Heilongjiang, and Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qianlong Emperor he served as Left Director of the Imperial Clan and as military governor at Guangzhou, Heilongjiang, and Mukden.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恪勤。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Keqin was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Keqin.

sentences.zh: 永曖四世孫福錕，事德宗，官至體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: Yongnuan's fourth-generation descendant Fuku, serving the Dezong, reached the office of Grand Secretary of the Pavilion Preserving Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Fuku, fourth-generation descendant of Yongnuan, served under the Guangxu Emperor and rose to Grand Secretary of the Pavilion Preserving Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文慎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Wenshen was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Wenshen.

sentences.zh: 誠隱郡王允祉，聖祖第三子。

translations.literal: Prince of the Commandery of Chengyin Yunzhi was the Holy Ancestor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yunzhi of Chengyin Commandery was the Kangxi Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十九年七月，偕皇太子詣古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山行宮，上命先還。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi, together with the crown prince he went to the imperial resort at Gurun Fuerjian Jia Hunga Mountain; the Emperor ordered him to return first.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kangxi 29 he accompanied the crown prince to the imperial lodge at Gurun Fuerjian Jia Hunga Mountain, but the Emperor ordered him to return ahead of them.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，闕里孔廟成，命偕皇四子往祭。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, when the Confucius Temple at Qufu was completed, he was ordered to go together with the fourth prince to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 32, when the Confucius Temple at Qufu was completed, he was ordered to go with the fourth prince to perform the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 凡行圍、謁陵，皆從。

translations.literal: Whenever there were hunting expeditions or tomb visits, he always followed.
translations.idiomatic: He always accompanied the Emperor on hunting expeditions and tomb visits.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征，允祉領鑲紅旗大營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the Emperor personally campaigned; Yunzhi commanded the great camp of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35, when the Emperor led the campaign in person, Yunzhi commanded the main camp of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，封誠郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 37 he was enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，敏妃之喪未百日，允祉薙髮，坐降貝勒，王府長史以下譴黜有差。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, before a hundred days had passed since Consort Min's mourning, Yunzhi shaved his head; for this he was demoted to beile, and the chief steward of the princely mansion and those below were rebuked and dismissed with varying penalties.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38, before the hundred-day mourning period for Consort Min had elapsed, Yunzhi shaved his head; he was demoted to beile, and the chief steward of his household and subordinate officials were dismissed with penalties of varying severity.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，命勘三門底柱。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was ordered to survey the pillar rocks at Sanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 43 he was ordered to inspect the pillar rocks at the Sanmen Gorge.

sentences.zh: 四十六年三月，迎上幸其邸園，侍宴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-sixth year he welcomed the Emperor to visit his mansion garden and attended the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 46 he welcomed the Emperor to his garden estate and waited upon him at a banquet.

sentences.zh: 嗣是，歲以為常，或一歲再幸。

translations.literal: From then on it became annual custom, sometimes twice in one year the Emperor would visit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it became an annual custom, and sometimes the Emperor visited twice in a single year.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，太子既廢，上以允祉與太子索親睦，召問太子情狀，且曰：「允祉與允礽雖暱，然未慫恿其為惡，故不罪也。」

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, after the crown prince had been deposed, because Yunzhi had always been close to the crown prince the Emperor summoned and questioned him about the crown prince's condition, and said: "Although Yunzhi and Yinreng are intimate, he did not instigate him to do evil, and therefore he is not punished."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 47, after the crown prince's deposition, the Emperor summoned Yunzhi, who had always been on close terms with the crown prince, to inquire about his conduct, and declared: "Though Yunzhi and Yinreng are close, he did not urge him toward wickedness, and so he goes unpunished."

sentences.zh: 蒙古喇嘛巴漢格隆為允禔厭勝廢太子，允祉偵得之，發其事。

translations.literal: The Mongol lama Ba Han Geleng performed sorcery for Yunzhi the First Prince to bring down the crown prince; Yunzhi discovered it through investigation and exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol lama Ba Han Geleng performed sorcery at the behest of Yunzhi, the First Prince, to destroy the crown prince; Yunzhi discovered this through investigation and exposed the plot.

sentences.zh: 明年，太子復立，允祉進封誠親王。

translations.literal: The next year the crown prince was again established and Yunzhi was advanced to Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the crown prince was reinstated, Yunzhi was promoted to Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀五千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 51 he was granted five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 聖祖邃律曆之學，命允祉率庶吉士何國宗等輯律呂、算法諸書，諭曰：「古歷規模甚好，但其數目歲久不合。

translations.literal: The Holy Ancestor was deeply versed in calendrical and astronomical learning; he ordered Yunzhi to lead junior compilers He Guozong and others to compile books on pitch pipes, musical tones, and calculation methods, instructing: "The ancient calendar's structure is very good, but its figures after many years no longer accord.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply versed in calendrical astronomy, the Kangxi Emperor ordered Yunzhi to lead junior compilers including He Guozong in compiling works on pitch pipes and calculation, instructing them: "The structure of the ancient calendar is excellent, but after so many years its figures no longer fit.

sentences.zh: 今修曆書，規模宜存古，數目宜準今。」

translations.literal: Now in revising the calendar book, the structure should preserve the ancient, and the figures should accord with the present."
translations.idiomatic: In revising the calendar now, preserve the ancient framework but adjust the figures to match present observations."

sentences.zh: 五十三年十一月，書成，奏進。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-third year the book was completed and memorialized for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kangxi 53 the work was completed and presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命以律呂、曆法、算法三者合為一書，名曰《律曆淵源》。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the three—pitch pipes and tones, calendar methods, and calculation methods—combined into one book, named 《Sources of Pitch Pipes and the Calendar》.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the three works on pitch pipes, calendrical methods, and calculation combined into a single book titled 《Sources of Pitch Pipes and the Calendar》.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，上有事於圜丘，拜畢，命允祉行禮。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year the Emperor performed rites at the Circular Altar; when the obeisance was finished he ordered Yunzhi to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58, after the Emperor performed rites at the Circular Altar and completed his obeisances, he ordered Yunzhi to conduct the ceremonial offerings.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，封子弘晟為世子，班俸視貝子。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year his son Hongcheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with stipend rank equal to beise.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 59 his son Hongcheng was named heir apparent, with stipend equal to that of a beise.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上命弘晟偕皇四子、皇十二子祭盛京三陵。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the Emperor ordered Hongcheng together with the fourth and twelfth princes to offer sacrifice at the three tombs of Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 60 the Emperor ordered Hongcheng, together with the fourth and twelfth princes, to perform sacrifices at the three imperial tombs at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命允祉守護景陵。

translations.literal: When the Shizong ascended the throne he ordered Yunzhi to guard the Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor ascended the throne he assigned Yunzhi to guard the Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，弘晟得罪，削世子，為閑散宗室。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng Hongcheng was convicted of an offense, stripped of heir status, and made a loose member of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 Hongcheng was found guilty of an offense, deprived of heir status, and reduced to unattached imperial clansman.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，允祉索蘇克濟賕，事發，在上前詰王大臣，上責其無臣禮，議奪爵，錮私第。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year Yunzhi extorted bribes from Sukeji; when the affair came to light he interrogated princes and great ministers before the Emperor; the Emperor rebuked him for lacking the propriety of a subject; stripping his rank was deliberated and he was confined in his private mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yongzheng 6 Yunzhi extorted bribes from Sukeji; when the scandal broke he cross-examined princes and ministers in the Emperor's presence; the Yongzheng Emperor rebuked him for gross insubordination, and after deliberation his title was to be stripped and he confined to his residence.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕止此一兄。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have only this one elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "He is my only surviving elder brother.

sentences.zh: 朕兄弟如允祉者何限？

translations.literal: My brothers like Yunzhi—how could they be limited in number?
translations.idiomatic: How many brothers like Yunzhi do I have?

sentences.zh: 皆欲激朕治其罪，其心誠不可喻。

translations.literal: All wish to provoke me to punish him for his crime—their hearts truly cannot be explained.
translations.idiomatic: They all mean to goad me into punishing him; their motives defy comprehension.

sentences.zh: 良亦朕不能感化所致，未可謂盡若輩之罪也。」

translations.literal: Yet it is also because I could not transform him by influence—it cannot be said that the fault lies entirely with those fellows."
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is also because I failed to reform him by example; the blame cannot be laid entirely on them."

sentences.zh: 命降郡王，而歸其罪於弘晟，交宗人府禁錮。

translations.literal: He ordered demotion to commandery prince, but placed the guilt upon Hongcheng and handed him to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yunzhi demoted to commandery prince but attributed the offense to Hongcheng, who was handed over to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，復進封親王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was again advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongzheng 8 he was restored to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 五月，怡親王之喪，允祉後至，無戚容。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, at Prince Yi's mourning, Yunzhi arrived late and had no sorrowful expression.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, at the mourning rites for Prince Yi, Yunzhi arrived late and showed no sign of grief.

sentences.zh: 莊親王允祿等劾，下宗人府議，奏稱：「允祉乖張不孝，暱近陳夢雷、周昌言，祈禳鎮魘，與阿其那、塞思黑、允禵交相黨附。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others impeached him; the case went to the Imperial Clan Court for deliberation; the memorial stated: "Yunzhi is perverse and unfilial, intimate with Chen Menglei and Zhou Changyan, performing prayers and sorcery to suppress and bewitch, and forming mutual faction with Aqina, Seshe, and Yinti.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yunlu and others impeached him; the Imperial Clan Court deliberated and reported: "Yunzhi is perverse and unfilial, consorts with Chen Menglei and Zhou Changyan, performs protective sorcery and curse rituals, and forms a faction with Aqina, Seshe, and Yinti.

sentences.zh: 其子弘晟凶頑狂縱，助父為惡，僅予禁錮，而允祉銜恨怨懟。

translations.literal: His son Hongcheng is fierce, obstinate, and wildly indulgent, aiding his father in evil; he was only given confinement, yet Yunzhi harbors resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongcheng is violent, stubborn, and unrestrained, abetting his father's wrongdoing; when Hongcheng received only confinement, Yunzhi nursed resentment and rage.

sentences.zh: 怡親王忠孝性成，允祉心懷嫉忌，並不懇請持服，王府齊集，遲至早散，背理蔑倫，當削爵。」

translations.literal: Prince Yi was filial and loyal by nature; Yunzhi harbored jealousy in his heart, and did not earnestly request to observe mourning dress; at the princely mansion assembly he arrived late and left early—against reason and scorning propriety—his rank should be stripped."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi was the soul of loyalty and filial piety; Yunzhi's heart was consumed with jealousy, and he did not earnestly ask to take up mourning garb; at the princely mansion gathering he came late and left early—contemptuous of duty and defiant of propriety—his title should be stripped."

sentences.zh: 與其子弘晟皆論死。

translations.literal: Both he and his son Hongcheng were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Both Yunzhi and his son Hongcheng were condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 上命奪爵，禁景山永安亭，聽家屬與偕，弘晟仍禁宗人府。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered his rank stripped, confinement at Yong'an Pavilion on Jingshan, allowing family members to accompany him; Hongcheng remained confined in the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yunzhi stripped of his title and confined at Yong'an Pavilion on Jingshan, permitting his family to accompany him; Hongcheng remained under confinement in the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 十年閏五月，薨，視郡王例殯葬。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year he died; burial followed commandery prince precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Yongzheng 10 he died and was interred with the honors due a commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，追諡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 a posthumous title was conferred upon him.

sentences.zh: 子弘暻，封貝子。

translations.literal: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as a beizi.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以不入八分輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were reduced step by step, with Bulwark of the State without the Eight Privileges perpetually inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants inherited in descending rank by precedent, eventually holding the title of Bulwark of the State without the Eight Privileges in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 五世孫載齡，襲爵。

translations.literal: Zailing, fifth-generation descendant, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Zailing, a fifth-generation descendant, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 事德宗，官至體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: Serving the Dezong, he reached the office of Grand Secretary of the Pavilion Preserving Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He served under the Guangxu Emperor and rose to Grand Secretary of the Pavilion Preserving Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文恪。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Wenke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted the posthumous title Wenke.

sentences.zh: 恒溫親王允祺，聖祖第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Hengwen Yunqi was the Holy Ancestor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yunqi, Hengwen, was the Kangxi Emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，上征噶爾丹，命允祺領正黃旗大營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi the Emperor campaigned against Galdan and ordered Yunqi to command the main camp of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35, when the Emperor marched against Galdan, he put Yunqi in command of the main camp of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 四十八年十月，封恒親王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as Prince Heng.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀五千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 51 he was granted five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，封子弘昇為世子，班祿視貝子。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year his son Hongsheng was enfeoffed as heir apparent, with salary equal to that of a beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58 his son Hongsheng was named heir apparent, with stipend equal to that of a beizi.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，坐事，削世子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, for an offense, heir-apparent status was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5, for an offense, he was stripped of heir-apparent status.

sentences.zh: 十年閏五月，允祺薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year Yunqi died; a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Yongzheng 10 Yunqi died and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子弘晊，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hongzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongzhi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong he died; posthumous title Ke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 40 and was granted the posthumous title Ke.

sentences.zh: 子永皓，襲郡王。

translations.literal: His son Yonghao inherited as commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yonghao succeeded as commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，薨，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year he died; posthumous title Jing was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 53 and was granted the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 弘升子永澤，襲貝子。

translations.literal: Hongsheng's son Yongze inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongsheng's son Yongze succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants by precedent were reduced step by step, with Defender of the State perpetually inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants inherited in descending rank by precedent, eventually holding the title of Defender of the State in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 弘昇既削世子，乾隆十九年卒，予貝勒品級，諡恭恪。

translations.literal: Hongsheng having already been stripped of heir-apparent status, in the nineteenth year of Qianlong he died; beile rank was granted, and posthumous title Gongke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongsheng had been stripped of heir-apparent status, he died in Qianlong 19; beile rank was posthumously granted, and he received the posthumous title Gongke.

sentences.zh: 淳度親王允祐，聖祖第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Chundu Yunyou was the Holy Ancestor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chundu was the Kangxi Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，上征噶爾丹，命允祐領鑲黃旗大營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi the Emperor campaigned against Galdan and ordered Yunyou to command the main camp of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
