translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35, when the Emperor marched against Galdan, he put Chundu in command of the main camp of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十七年三月，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 37 he was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 四十八年十月，封淳郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of the Commandery of Chun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chun Commandery.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀五千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year five thousand taels of silver were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 51 he was granted five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五十七年十月，正藍旗滿洲都統延信征西陲，命允祐管正藍三旗事務。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifty-seventh year, as Banner Commander Yanxin of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus campaigned on the western frontier, Yunyou was ordered to manage the affairs of the three Plain Blue banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 57, when Banner Commander Yanxin of the Plain Blue Banner Manchus marched on the western frontier, Chundu was ordered to administer the affairs of the three Plain Blue banners.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，進封親王，詔褒其安分守己，敬順小心。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was advanced to prince; an edict praised him for keeping within his station, respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was advanced to prince; an edict praised him for knowing his place, remaining dutiful, and conducting himself with careful reverence.

sentences.zh: 復命與誠親王允祉並書景陵碑額，以兩王皆工書故。

translations.literal: He was again ordered, together with Prince Chen Cheng Yin Yunzhi, to inscribe the stele for the Jing Mausoleum, because both princes were skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered, together with Prince Yunzhi, Chengyin, to inscribe the stele for the Jing Mausoleum, since both princes excelled at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year he died; a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongzheng 8 he died and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子弘曙。

translations.literal: His son Hongshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hongshu.

sentences.zh: 聖祖命皇十四子允禵為撫遠大將軍，駐甘州，令弘曙從。

translations.literal: The Holy Ancestor appointed the fourteenth son Yinti as Pacification Commissioner-General, stationed at Ganzhou, and ordered Hongshu to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor appointed the fourteenth son, Yinti, Pacification Commissioner-General, with headquarters at Ganzhou, and ordered Hongshu to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 聖祖崩，世宗召還京，封世子。

translations.literal: When the Holy Ancestor died, the Shizong summoned them back to the capital and enfeoffed Hongshu as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor died, the Yongzheng Emperor recalled them to Beijing and enfeoffed Hongshu as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，坐事削，改封弘暻為世子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, for an offense he was stripped of the title; Hongjing was enfeoffed as heir apparent in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5, for an offense, Hongshu was stripped of heir-apparent status, and Hongjing was enfeoffed as heir apparent in his stead.

sentences.zh: 允祐薨，弘暻襲。

translations.literal: When Yunyou died, Hongjing inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Chundu died, Hongjing succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十二年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Qianlong he died; posthumous title Shen was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 42 and was granted the posthumous title Shen.

sentences.zh: 子永鋆，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yongjun inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongjun succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were reduced step by step, with Defender of the State perpetually inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants inherited in descending rank, eventually holding the title of Defender of the State in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 永鋆子綿洵，事穆宗，官涼州副都統。

translations.literal: Yongjun's son Mianxun served the Muzong and held the office of Vice Banner Commander at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjun's son Mianxun served under the Tongzhi Emperor as Vice Banner Commander at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉戰河南、直隸、山東、湖北，克臨清，破連鎮、馮官屯，皆有功。

translations.literal: Fighting through Henan, Zhili, Shandong, and Hubei, he captured Linqing and broke Lianzhen and Fengguantun, distinguishing himself in each.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning through Henan, Zhili, Shandong, and Hubei, he took Linqing and routed the enemy at Lianzhen and Fengguantun, earning merit in each engagement.

sentences.zh: 遷荊州將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡莊武。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Zhuangwu was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was granted the posthumous title Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 允禩，聖祖第八子。

translations.literal: Yinsi was the Holy Ancestor's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi was the Kangxi Emperor's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年三月，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirty-seventh year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 37 he was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月，署內務府總管事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the forty-seventh year he was appointed acting director-general of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Kangxi 47 he was appointed acting director-general of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 太子允礽既廢，允禩謀代立。

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yinsi plotted to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Yinreng had been deposed, Yinsi plotted to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 諸皇子允禟、允䄉、允禵，諸大臣阿靈阿、鄂倫岱、揆敘、王鴻緒等，皆附允禩。

translations.literal: The princes Yunsi, Yun'e, and Yinti, and the great ministers Aling'a, Erlun Dai, Kuixu, Wang Hongxu, and others, all sided with Yinsi.
translations.idiomatic: The princes Yunsi, Yun'e, and Yinti, together with the senior ministers Aling'a, Erlun Dai, Kuixu, Wang Hongxu, and others, all rallied to Yinsi.

sentences.zh: 允禔言於上，謂相士張明德言允禩後必大貴，上大怒，會內務府總管凌普以附太子得罪，籍其家，允禩頗庇之，上以責允禩。

translations.literal: Yunzhi spoke to the Emperor, saying the diviner Zhang Mingde had declared that Yinsi was destined for great eminence; the Emperor was greatly angered. At the same time Ling Pu, director-general of the Imperial Household Department, had been punished for siding with the crown prince and his property was confiscated; Yinsi had sheltered him considerably, and the Emperor rebuked Yinsi.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhi reported to the Emperor that the diviner Zhang Mingde had declared Yinsi destined for the highest fortune; the Emperor flew into a rage. At the same time Ling Pu, director-general of the Imperial Household Department, was punished for siding with the crown prince and his estate was confiscated; Yinsi had sheltered him at length, and the Emperor rebuked Yinsi for it.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「凌普貪婪巨富，所籍未盡，允禩每妄博虛名，凡朕所施恩澤，俱歸功於己，是又一太子矣！

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Ling Pu is rapaciously wealthy; what was confiscated does not exhaust his holdings. Yinsi constantly seeks hollow reputation—whenever I bestow favors, he claims the credit for himself. He is another crown prince!
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Ling Pu is greedily wealthy beyond measure, and what was confiscated does not exhaust his holdings. Yinsi constantly trades on empty reputation: every favor I bestow, he claims as his own doing. He is another crown prince!

sentences.zh: 如有人譽允禩，必殺無赦。」

translations.literal: If anyone praises Yinsi, he shall be executed without mercy."
translations.idiomatic: If anyone praises Yinsi, he shall be put to death without mercy."

sentences.zh: 翌日，召諸皇子入，諭曰：「當廢允礽時，朕即諭諸皇子有鑽營為皇太子者，即國之賊，法所不容。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned the princes and declared: "When Yinreng was deposed, I immediately told all the princes that whoever schemed to become crown prince was an enemy of the state, whom the law would not spare.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned the princes and declared: "When Yinreng was deposed, I immediately warned every prince that whoever schemed to become crown prince was an enemy of the state, whom the law would not spare.

sentences.zh: 允禩柔姦性成，妄蓄大志，黨羽相結，謀害允礽。

translations.literal: Yinsi is by nature soft and treacherous; he harbors grand ambitions without warrant; his faction binds together and plots against Yinreng.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi is treacherous by nature; he harbors unwarranted ambition; his partisans have bound together and plotted against Yinreng.

sentences.zh: 今其事皆敗露，即鎖系，交議政處審理。」

translations.literal: Now the whole affair has come to light; he was immediately placed in chains and referred to the Deliberative Princes for trial."
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole affair has come to light; he was immediately placed in chains and referred to the Deliberative Princes for judgment."

sentences.zh: 允禟語允禵，入為允禩營救，上怒，出佩刀將誅允禵；

translations.literal: Yunsi spoke to Yinti, who went in to plead for Yinsi; the Emperor raged, drew his sword, and was about to execute Yinti;
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi spoke to Yinti, who went in to plead for Yinsi; the Emperor flew into a rage, drew his sword, and was about to kill Yinti;

sentences.zh: 允祺跪抱勸止，上怒少解，仍諭諸皇子、議政大臣等毋寬允禩罪。

translations.literal: Yunqi knelt and held him back, pleading; the Emperor's anger eased somewhat, but he still instructed the princes and deliberative ministers not to lenient toward Yinsi's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Yunqi knelt and held him back, pleading with him to stop; the Emperor's anger eased somewhat, yet he still instructed the princes and deliberative ministers not to be lenient toward Yinsi's offense.

sentences.zh: 逮相士張明德會鞫，詞連順承郡王布穆巴，公賴士、普奇，順承郡王長史阿祿。

translations.literal: When the diviner Zhang Mingde was arrested and jointly interrogated, his testimony implicated Prince of the Commandery of Shuncheng Bumuba, Gong Laishi, Puqi, and Shuncheng commandery prince chief steward Alu.
translations.idiomatic: When the diviner Zhang Mingde was arrested and interrogated jointly, his testimony implicated Prince Bumuba of Shuncheng Commandery, Gong Laishi, Puqi, and the chief steward of the Shuncheng commandery prince, Alu.

sentences.zh: 張明德坐凌遲處死，普奇奪公爵，允禩亦奪貝勒，為閑散宗室。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingde was sentenced to death by slicing; Puqi was stripped of duke rank; Yinsi was also stripped of beile rank and reduced to idle status among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingde was sentenced to death by dismemberment; Puqi was stripped of his ducal rank; Yinsi was also stripped of beile rank and reduced to idle status within the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 上復諭諸皇子曰：「允禩庇其乳母夫雅齊布，雅齊布之叔厩長吳達理與御史雍泰同榷關稅，不相能，訴之允禩，允禩借事痛責雍泰。

translations.literal: The Emperor again addressed the princes: "Yinsi sheltered his wet-nurse's husband Yaqibu. Yaqibu's uncle, stable chief Wu Dali, collected transit tax duties together with Censor Yong Tai; they could not get along, and Wu complained to Yinsi, who seized the occasion to beat Yong Tai severely.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again addressed the princes: "Yinsi sheltered his wet-nurse's husband Yaqibu. Yaqibu's uncle, the stable chief Wu Dali, collected transit tax duties together with Censor Yong Tai; the two could not abide each other, and Wu complained to Yinsi, who seized the occasion to punish Yong Tai harshly.

sentences.zh: 朕聞之，以雅齊布發翁牛特公主處。

translations.literal: When I heard of it, I sent Yaqibu away to the Ongniot Princess's estate.
translations.idiomatic: When I learned of it, I sent Yaqibu away to serve at the Ongniot Princess's estate.

sentences.zh: 允禩因怨朕，與褚英孫蘇努相結，敗壞國事。

translations.literal: Yinsi therefore resented me and allied with Sunu, grandson of Tuying, undermining state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi therefore resented me and allied with Sunu, grandson of Tuying, to the ruin of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 允禩又受制於妻，妻為安郡王岳樂甥，嫉妒行惡，是以允禩尚未生子。

translations.literal: Yinsi is also controlled by his wife; she is a niece of Prince of the Commandery of An Yuele, jealous and wicked in conduct, which is why Yinsi has not yet had a son.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi is also ruled by his wife, a niece of Prince Yuele of An Commandery, jealous and vicious in conduct, which is why Yinsi has not yet had a son.

sentences.zh: 此皆爾曹所知，爾曹當遵朕旨，方是為臣子之理；

translations.literal: All of this you yourselves know; you should follow my commands—only thus is the way of subject and son;
translations.idiomatic: All of this you know yourselves; you must follow my commands—only thus is the way of loyal subject and dutiful son;

sentences.zh: 若不如此存心，日後朕考終，必至將朕躬置乾清宮內，束甲相爭耳。」

translations.literal: if you do not think thus, after my death you will surely put my person in the Qianqing Palace and fight in armor against one another."
translations.idiomatic: if you do not set your hearts thus, after my death you will surely lay my body in the Qianqing Palace and fight one another in armor."

sentences.zh: 上幸南苑，遘疾，還宮，召允禩入見，並召太子使居咸安宮。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited the Southern Park and fell ill; returning to the palace, he summoned Yinsi for an audience and also summoned the crown prince to reside at Xian'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited the Southern Park and fell ill; on returning to the palace he summoned Yinsi for an audience and also ordered the crown prince to reside at Xian'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上命諸大臣於諸皇子中舉可為太子者，阿靈阿等私示意諸大臣舉允禩。

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor ordered the great ministers to nominate among the princes who could serve as crown prince; Aling'a and others privately signaled the great ministers to nominate Yinsi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Emperor ordered the senior ministers to nominate from among the princes one fit to be crown prince; Aling'a and others privately signaled the ministers to nominate Yinsi.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「允禩未更事，且罹罪，其母亦微賤，宜別舉。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Yinsi has not yet managed affairs of state, and has moreover been punished; his mother is also of low birth. Another should be nominated."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Yinsi has not yet held office, and has moreover been punished; his mother is also of humble birth. Another should be nominated."

sentences.zh: 上釋允礽，亦復允禩貝勒。

translations.literal: The Emperor released Yinreng and also restored Yinsi as beile.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor released Yinreng and also restored Yinsi to beile rank.

sentences.zh: 四十八年正月，上召諸大臣，問倡舉允禩為太子者，諸臣不敢質言。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-eighth year the Emperor summoned the great ministers and asked who had advocated nominating Yinsi as crown prince; the ministers dared not speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kangxi 48 the Emperor summoned the senior ministers and asked who had advocated nominating Yinsi as crown prince; the ministers dared not speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 上以大學士馬齊先言眾欲舉允禩，因譴馬齊，不復深詰。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Grand Secretary Ma Qi had been the first to say the multitude wished to nominate Yinsi, rebuked Ma Qi and did not pursue the matter further.
translations.idiomatic: Because Grand Secretary Ma Qi had been the first to say the assembly wished to nominate Yinsi, the Emperor rebuked Ma Qi and did not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 尋復立允礽為太子。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Yinreng was re-established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Yinreng was reinstated as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 五十一年十一月，复廢允礽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year Yinreng was deposed again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kangxi 51 Yinreng was deposed again.

sentences.zh: 六十一年十一月，上疾大漸，召允禩及諸皇子允祉、允祐、允禟、允䄉、允祹、允祥同受末命。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixty-first year, as the Emperor's illness grew critical, he summoned Yinsi together with the princes Yunzhi, Yunyou, Yunsi, Yun'e, Yuntao, and Yinxiang to receive his final commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kangxi 61, as the Emperor's illness grew critical, he summoned Yinsi together with the princes Yunzhi, Chundu, Yunsi, Yun'e, Yuntao, and Yinxiang to receive his final commands.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命允禩總理事務，進封廉親王，授理籓院尚書。

translations.literal: When the Shizong ascended the throne, he ordered Yinsi to supervise overall administration, advanced him to Prince Lian, and appointed him Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor ascended the throne, he put Yinsi in charge of overall administration, advanced him to Prince Lian, and appointed him Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命辦理工部事務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was ordered to administer Ministry of Works affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was ordered to administer Ministry of Works affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇太子允礽之廢也，允禩謀繼立，世宗深憾之。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yinreng was deposed, Yinsi had plotted to succeed him; the Shizong deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yinreng was deposed, Yinsi had plotted to succeed him; the Yongzheng Emperor deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 允禩亦知世宗憾之深也，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Yinsi also knew how deeply the Shizong resented him, and was chronically dispirited.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi also knew how deeply the Yongzheng Emperor resented him, and was chronically dispirited.

sentences.zh: 封親王命下，其福晉烏雅氏對賀者曰：「何賀為？

translations.literal: When the decree enfeoffing him as prince was issued, his consort, Lady Uya, said to those offering congratulations: "What is there to congratulate?
translations.idiomatic: When the order enfeoffing him as prince arrived, his primary consort, Lady Uya, said to those who came to congratulate her: "What is there to congratulate?

sentences.zh: 慮不免首領耳！」

translations.literal: I fear we shall not keep our heads!"
translations.idiomatic: I fear we shall not escape with our lives!"

sentences.zh: 語聞，世宗憾滋甚。

translations.literal: When word of this reached him, the Shizong's resentment grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: When word of this reached him, the Yongzheng Emperor's resentment grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 會副都統祁爾薩條奏：「滿洲俗遇喪，親友饋粥吊慰。

translations.literal: Then Vice Banner Commander Qi'ersa memorialized item by item: "By Manchu custom, when there is bereavement, relatives and friends bring congee in condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Then Vice Banner Commander Qi'ersa submitted a detailed memorial: "By Manchu custom, when there is bereavement, relatives and friends bring congee in condolence.

sentences.zh: 後風俗漸弛，大設奢饌，過事奢靡。」

translations.literal: Later the custom gradually lapsed; lavish feasts were spread and extravagance carried to excess."
translations.idiomatic: Later the custom gradually lapsed; lavish feasts were spread and mourning was carried to wasteful excess."

sentences.zh: 上用其議申禁，因諭斥：「允禩居母妃喪，沽孝名，百日後猶扶掖匍匐而行；

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted his proposal and issued a prohibition, and further denounced: "During mourning for his consort's mother, Yinsi traded on the name of filial piety; even after the hundred days he still leaned on others' support and crawled along the ground;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor adopted his proposal and issued a prohibition, and further denounced: "During mourning for his consort's mother, Yinsi traded on the name of filial piety; even after the hundred days he still leaned on others for support and crawled along the ground;

sentences.zh: 而允䄉，允禟、允指稱饋食，大肆筵席，皇考諭責者屢矣。」

translations.literal: yet Yun'e, Yunsi, and Yuntao claimed to be bringing food in condolence and held banquets on a grand scale—our late father had repeatedly rebuked this."
translations.idiomatic: yet Yun'e, Yunsi, and Yuntao claimed to be bringing condolence food and held banquets on a grand scale—our late father had repeatedly rebuked this."

sentences.zh: 二年，上諭曰：「允禩素行陰狡，皇考所深知，降旨不可悉數。

translations.literal: In the second year the Emperor declared: "Yinsi has always been secretly crafty—a thing our late father knew full well, and the edicts he sent down on the subject cannot all be counted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Emperor declared: "Yinsi has always been secretly crafty—a thing our late father knew full well, and the edicts he issued on the subject cannot all be counted.

sentences.zh: 自朕即位，優封親王，任以總理事務。

translations.literal: Since my accession I have graciously enfeoffed him as prince and entrusted him with overall administration.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne I have generously enfeoffed him as prince and put him in charge of overall administration.

sentences.zh: 乃不能輸其誠悃以輔朕躬，懷挾私心，至今未已。

translations.literal: Yet he could not offer his sincere devotion to assist me, but harbors private designs that continue to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not offer sincere devotion to assist me, but harbors private designs that continue to this day.

sentences.zh: 凡事欲激朕怒以治其罪，加朕以不令之名。

translations.literal: In everything he seeks to provoke my anger so that I may punish him, thereby attaching an ill name to me.
translations.idiomatic: In every matter he seeks to goad my anger so that I may punish him, thereby casting an ill name upon me.

sentences.zh: 允禩在諸弟中頗有治事材，朕甚愛惜之，非允禟、允䄉等可比，是以屢加教誨，令其改過，不但成朕友於之誼，亦全前三復教誨之理？

translations.literal: Among my younger brothers Yinsi possesses considerable talent for administration, and I greatly cherish him—not comparable to Yunsi, Yun'e, and the like; therefore I have repeatedly admonished him and urged him to reform—not only to fulfill my brotherly duty, but also to complete the principle of thrice-repeated admonitions?
translations.idiomatic: Among my younger brothers Yinsi possesses considerable talent for administration, and I cherish him greatly—he is not to be compared with Yunsi, Yun'e, and the like. That is why I have repeatedly admonished him and urged him to reform: not only to fulfill my duty toward my brothers, but also to honor my late father's principle of thrice-repeated admonitions?

sentences.zh: 朕一身上關宗廟社稷，不得不為？

translations.literal: On my single person hangs relation to the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain—I cannot but act?
translations.idiomatic: On my single person hang the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of state—can I not act?

sentences.zh: 皇考慈愛之衷。

translations.literal: The late Emperor's loving heart.
translations.idiomatic: According to my late father's loving heart.

sentences.zh: 朕果欲治其罪，豈有於防範。

translations.literal: If I truly wished to punish his crimes, would there be laxity in guard?
translations.idiomatic: If I truly intended to punish his crimes, would I have been lax in guarding against him?

sentences.zh: 允禩在皇考時，恣意妄行，匪伊朝夕，朕可不念祖宗肇造鴻圖，以永貽子孫之安乎？」

translations.literal: During our late father's reign Yinsi acted willfully and recklessly—not for one day only; can I fail to remember how our forebears established this great enterprise, and secure lasting peace for our descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: During our late father's reign Yinsi acted willfully and recklessly—not for a single day only; can I fail to remember how our forebears established this great enterprise, and secure lasting peace for our descendants?"

sentences.zh: 三年二月，三年服滿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year the three-year mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongzheng 3 the three-year mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 以允禩任總理事務，挾私懷詐，有罪無功，不予議敘。

translations.literal: Because Yinsi in supervising overall administration harbored private designs and deceit, guilty without merit, he was granted no deliberation for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yinsi, while supervising overall administration, harbored private designs and deceit, being guilty without merit, he was granted no deliberation for rewards.

sentences.zh: 尋因工部製祈榖壇祖宗神牌草率，阿爾泰駐兵軍器粗窳，屢下詔詰責允禩；

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because spirit tablets for the Prayer for Grain altar at the Ministry of Works had been made carelessly, and Altai's garrison weapons were crude and shoddy, edicts repeatedly rebuked Yinsi;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because spirit tablets for the Prayer for Grain altar at the Ministry of Works had been made carelessly, and the weapons of Altai's garrison were crude and shoddy, edicts repeatedly rebuked Yinsi;

sentences.zh: 允禩議減內務府披甲，上令覆奏，又請一佐領增甲九十餘副。

translations.literal: Yinsi proposed reducing the armor quota of the Imperial Household Department; the Emperor ordered a memorial in reply, and he then requested one company commander to add more than ninety sets of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi proposed reducing the armor quota of the Imperial Household Department; the Emperor ordered a memorial in reply, and he then requested that one company commander add more than ninety sets of armor.

sentences.zh: 上以允禩前後異議，諭謂：「陰邪叵測，莫此為甚！」

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Yinsi's views before and after contradicted each other, declared: "Secret evil beyond measure—nothing surpasses this!"
translations.idiomatic: Because Yinsi's views before and after contradicted each other, the Emperor declared: "Secret treachery beyond fathoming—nothing surpasses this!"

sentences.zh: 因命一佐領留甲五十副不即裁，待缺出不補。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered one company commander to retain fifty sets of armor without immediate reduction; when vacancies occurred they would not be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered one company commander to keep fifty sets of armor and not cut them immediately; when posts fell vacant they would not be filled.

sentences.zh: 隸內務府披甲諸人集允禩邸囂閧，翌日，又集副都統李延禧家，且縱掠。

translations.literal: The men assigned to the Imperial Household Department's armor quota gathered at Yinsi's mansion in uproar; the next day they gathered again at Vice Banner Commander Li Yanxi's home, and even plundered at will.
translations.idiomatic: The armor-bearers under the Imperial Household Department mobbed Yinsi's mansion in uproar; the next day they mobbed Vice Banner Commander Li Yanxi's home as well, looting as they went.

sentences.zh: 上命捕治，諸人自列允禩使閧延禧家，允禩不置辯。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered them arrested and punished; the men themselves testified that Yinsi had sent them to riot at Yanxi's home, and Yinsi made no defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered them arrested and punished; the men themselves testified that Yinsi had sent them to riot at Li Yanxi's home, and Yinsi offered no defense.

sentences.zh: 上命允禩鞫定為首者立斬，允禩以五人姓名上，上察其一乃自首，其一堅稱病未往，責允禩所讞不實。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Yinsi to try the case and designate the ringleaders for immediate execution; Yinsi submitted the names of five men; the Emperor discovered that one had turned himself in and one steadfastly claimed he had been ill and had not gone; he rebuked Yinsi because the indictment was not true.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Yinsi to try the case and designate the ringleaders for immediate execution. Yinsi submitted five names, but the Emperor found that one man had turned himself in and another steadfastly insisted he had been too ill to go. He rebuked Yinsi for a false indictment.

sentences.zh: 宗人府議奪允禩爵，上命寬之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court deliberated stripping Yinsi of his rank; the Emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court deliberated stripping Yinsi of his rank, but the Emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 允禩杖殺護軍九十六，命太監閻倫隱其事，厚賜之。

translations.literal: Yinsi beat to death ninety-six guards, ordered the eunuch Yan Lun to conceal the matter, and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi had ninety-six guards beaten to death, then ordered the eunuch Yan Lun to cover it up and richly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 宗人府复議奪允禩爵，上复寬之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court again deliberated stripping Yinsi of his rank; the Emperor again ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court again deliberated stripping Yinsi of his rank, and the Emperor again showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，上御西暖閣，召諸王大臣暴允禩罪狀，略曰：「當時允禩希冀非望，欲沽忠孝之名，而事事傷聖祖之心。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the Emperor presided at the West Warm Pavilion, summoned the princes and senior ministers to expose Yinsi's crimes, stating in summary: "At that time Yinsi harbored improper ambitions, sought to purchase a reputation for loyalty and filial piety, yet in every matter wounded the Holy Ancestor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, the Emperor presided at the West Warm Pavilion and summoned the princes and senior ministers to expose Yinsi's crimes. He declared in summary: "At that time Yinsi harbored improper ambitions and sought to purchase a reputation for loyalty and filial piety, yet in every matter he wounded the Kangxi Emperor's heart.

sentences.zh: 二阿哥坐廢，聖祖命朕與允禩在京辦事，凡有啟奏，皆蒙御批，由允禩藏貯。

translations.literal: When the Second Prince was deposed, the Holy Ancestor ordered me and Yinsi to handle affairs in the capital; every memorial received imperial marginalia, which Yinsi kept in store.
translations.idiomatic: When the Second Prince was deposed, the Kangxi Emperor ordered me and Yinsi to handle affairs in the capital. Every memorial received imperial marginalia, and Yinsi kept them in store.

sentences.zh: 嗣問允禩，則曰：'前值皇考怒，恐不測，故焚毀筆札，禦批亦納其中。

translations.literal: Later when I asked Yinsi, he said: 'Previously, when Our Late Father was angry, fearing the unpredictable, I therefore burned letters and notes; the imperial marginalia were included therein as well.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when I asked Yinsi, he said: 'When Our Late Father was angry before, I feared what might happen, so I burned the letters and notes—and the imperial marginalia were among them.

sentences.zh: '此允禩親向朕言者。

translations.literal: This is what Yinsi personally told me.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Yinsi personally told me.

sentences.zh: 聖祖升遐，朕念允禩夙有才幹，冀其痛改其非，為國家出力，令其總理事務，加封親王，推心置腹。

translations.literal: When the Holy Ancestor passed away, I recalled Yinsi's long-standing talent and ability, hoped he would deeply reform his faults and serve the state, had him oversee general affairs, promoted him to qinwang, and treated him with complete trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor passed away, I recalled Yinsi's long-standing talent and hoped he would thoroughly reform and serve the state. I had him oversee general affairs, promoted him to qinwang, and treated him with complete trust.

sentences.zh: 三年以來，宗人府及諸大臣劾議，什伯累積，朕百端容忍，乃允禩詭譎陰邪，狂妄悖亂，包藏禍心，日益加甚。

translations.literal: Over three years, the Imperial Clan Court and senior ministers impeached and deliberated, piling up scores upon scores; I tolerated him in every way, yet Yinsi was deceitful and secretly wicked, arrogant and rebellious, harboring evil intent, growing worse by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years the Imperial Clan Court and senior ministers impeached him again and again, piling up scores of charges. I tolerated him in every way I could, yet Yinsi remained deceitful and secretly wicked, arrogant and rebellious, harboring evil intent and growing worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 朕令宗人府訊問何得將皇考禦批焚毀，允禩改言：'抱病昏昧，誤行燒毀。

translations.literal: I ordered the Imperial Clan Court to interrogate him as to how he could have burned Our Late Father's marginalia; Yinsi changed his story: 'While ill, in a confused state, I mistakenly burned them.
translations.idiomatic: I ordered the Imperial Clan Court to ask how he could have burned Our Late Father's marginalia. Yinsi changed his story: 'While ill and confused, I mistakenly burned them.

sentences.zh: '及朕面質之，公然設誓，詛及一家。

translations.literal: When I confronted him face to face, he openly swore oaths, cursing my whole family.
translations.idiomatic: When I confronted him face to face, he openly swore oaths and cursed my whole family.

sentences.zh: 允禩自絕於天，自絕於祖宗，自絕於朕，斷不可留於宗姓之內，為我朝之玷！

translations.literal: Yinsi has cut himself off from Heaven, from the ancestors, and from me; he absolutely cannot remain within the clan surname—he would be a stain upon our dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi has cut himself off from Heaven, from the ancestors, and from me. He absolutely cannot remain within the imperial clan—he would be a stain upon our dynasty!

sentences.zh: 謹述皇考諭，遵先朝削籍離宗之典，革去允禩黃帶子，以儆兇邪，為萬世子孫鑑戒。」

translations.literal: I respectfully relate Our Late Father's instruction: following the precedent of earlier reigns for striking from the register and leaving the clan, Yinsi's yellow girdle is removed, to warn the vicious and wicked, as a lesson for all posterity."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully relate Our Late Father's instruction: following earlier precedents for striking a man from the register and removing him from the clan, Yinsi's yellow girdle is removed—to warn the vicious and wicked and to serve as a lesson for all posterity."

sentences.zh: 並命逐其福晉還外家。

translations.literal: He also ordered Yinsi's primary consort sent back to her natal home.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Yinsi's primary consort sent back to her natal family.

sentences.zh: 二月，授允禩為民王，不留所屬佐領人員，凡朝會，視民公、侯、伯例，稱親王允禩。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yinsi was made a commoner prince; his company commanders and subordinates were not retained; at audiences he was treated like commoner dukes, marquises, and earls, and addressed as Prince Yinsi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yinsi was made a commoner prince. His company commanders and subordinates were not retained. At court audiences he was treated like commoner dukes, marquises, and earls, and still addressed as Prince Yinsi.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣請誅允禩，上不許。

translations.literal: The princes and senior ministers requested Yinsi's execution; the Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers asked that Yinsi be executed, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋命削王爵，交宗人府圈禁高牆。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered stripped of princely rank and handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement within high walls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was stripped of princely rank and handed to the Imperial Clan Court for confinement within high walls.

sentences.zh: 宗人府請更名編入佐領：​​允禩改名阿其那，子弘旺改菩薩保。

translations.literal: The Imperial Clan Court requested a change of name and assignment to a company register: Yinsi was renamed Aqina, his son Hongwang Pusabao.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court requested that he be renamed and entered on a company register: Yinsi was renamed Aqina, and his son Hongwang was renamed Pusabao.

sentences.zh: 六月，諸王大臣复臚允禩罪狀四十事，請與允禟、允並正典刑，上暴其罪於中外。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the princes and senior ministers again enumerated forty counts in Yinsi's indictment, requested that he, Yunsi, and Yun be punished by proper law; the Emperor exposed their crimes at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the princes and senior ministers again enumerated forty counts against Yinsi and asked that he, Yunsi, and Yinti be punished according to law. The Emperor exposed their crimes throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 九月，允禩患嘔噦，命給與調養，未幾卒於幽所。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yinsi suffered vomiting and hiccups; he was ordered given care; before long he died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yinsi suffered vomiting and hiccups. He was ordered given medical care, but before long he died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣仍請戮屍，不許。

translations.literal: The princes and senior ministers again requested posthumous dismemberment; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers again asked that his corpse be dismembered, but this was not granted.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年正月，高宗諭曰：「聖祖第八子允禩，第九子允禟結黨妄行，罪皆自取。

translations.literal: In the first month of Qianlong 43, the Gaozong declared: "The Holy Ancestor's eighth son Yinsi and ninth son Yunsi formed factions and acted recklessly; their guilt was entirely of their own making.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 43, the Qianlong Emperor declared: "The Kangxi Emperor's eighth son Yinsi and ninth son Yunsi formed factions and acted recklessly; they brought their guilt upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 皇考僅令削籍更名，以示愧辱。

translations.literal: Our Late Father only ordered them struck from the register and renamed, to show shame and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Our Late Father only ordered them struck from the register and renamed, to mark their shame and disgrace.

sentences.zh: 就兩人心術而論，覬覦窺竊，誠所不免，及皇考紹登大寶。

translations.literal: Judging the two men's inner disposition, covert longing and secret scheming truly could not be avoided; and when Our Late Father succeeded to the Great Treasure—
translations.idiomatic: Judging the two men's inner disposition, covert longing and secret scheming could hardly be avoided. Yet once Our Late Father succeeded to the throne—

sentences.zh: 皇考晚年屢向朕諭及，愀然不樂，意頗悔，

translations.literal: In his later years Our Late Father repeatedly spoke to me of this, grim and unhappy, his mind rather regretful,
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Our Late Father often spoke to me of this, grim and unhappy, his mind full of regret.

sentences.zh: 怨尤誹謗，亦情事所有，特未有顯然悖逆之之，若將有待。

translations.literal: resentment, complaints, and slander were also matters within reason; only there was no clearly rebellious act, if one waits [text corrupted], as though something were still awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment, complaints, and slander were also to be expected; only there was no clearly rebellious act, as though something were still being held in reserve.

sentences.zh: 朕今臨御四十三年矣，此事重大，朕若不言，後世子孫無敢言者。

translations.literal: I have now reigned forty-three years; this matter is weighty; if I do not speak, no descendant in later ages will dare speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: I have now reigned forty-three years. This matter is too weighty: if I do not speak of it now, no descendant in later ages will dare to do so.

sentences.zh: 允禩、允禟仍復原名，收入玉牒，子孫一併？

translations.literal: Yinsi and Yunsi shall have their original names restored and be entered in the imperial genealogy; their descendants likewise all?
translations.idiomatic: Yinsi and Yunsi shall have their original names restored and be entered in the imperial genealogy, and their descendants shall be entered as well.

sentences.zh: 入。

translations.literal: Entered.
translations.idiomatic: They were entered therein.

sentences.zh: 此實仰體皇考仁心，申未竟之緒，想在天之靈​​亦當愉慰也。」

translations.literal: This truly accords with Our Late Father's humane heart, carrying out what was left unfinished; I trust his spirit in Heaven will also find solace."
translations.idiomatic: This truly accords with Our Late Father's humane heart and carries out what he left unfinished. I trust his spirit in Heaven will also be comforted."

sentences.zh: 允禟，聖祖第九子。

translations.literal: Yunsi was the Holy Ancestor's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi was the Kangxi Emperor's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十七年，上責允禩，允禟語允，入為保奏，上怒。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 47, the Emperor rebuked Yinsi; Yunsi spoke to Yun, who went in to plead on his behalf; the Emperor grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 47 the Emperor rebuked Yinsi. Yunsi spoke to Yinti, who went in to plead for him; the Emperor grew angry.

sentences.zh: 是時，上每巡幸，輒隨。

translations.literal: At this time, whenever the Emperor went on inspection tours, Yunsi accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, whenever the Emperor went on inspection tours, Yunsi accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 四十八年三月，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-eighth year he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 十月，命往翁牛特送和碩慍恪公主之喪。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to Wengniute to convey the funeral of Princess Hesuo Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was ordered to Wengniute to escort the funeral of Princess Hesuo Wenge.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀四千。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, four thousand taels of silver were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，世宗召允回京，以諸王大臣議，命允禟出駐西寧。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 1, the Shizong summoned Yun back to the capital; on deliberation by the princes and senior ministers, Yunsi was ordered to take station at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 the Yongzheng Emperor summoned Yinti back to the capital. On deliberation by the princes and senior ministers, Yunsi was ordered to take station at Xining.

sentences.zh: 允禟屢請緩行，上譴責所屬太監，允禟行至軍。

translations.literal: Yunsi repeatedly requested delay in departing; the Emperor rebuked the eunuchs under him; Yunsi traveled to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi repeatedly asked to delay his departure. The Emperor rebuked the eunuchs under him, and Yunsi set out for his post.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，宗人府劾允禟擅遣人至河州買草、勘牧地，違法肆行，請奪爵，上命寬之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunsi for sending men on his own authority to Hezhou to buy fodder and survey pasture lands, acting lawlessly; they requested stripping his rank; the Emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunsi for sending men on his own authority to Hezhou to buy fodder and survey pasture lands, acting lawlessly. They asked that his rank be stripped, but the Emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 三年，上聞允禟縱容家下人在西寧生事，遣都統楚宗往約束，楚宗至，允禟不出迎，傳旨詰責，曰：「上責我皆是，我復何言？

translations.literal: In the third year, learning that Yunsi indulged his household servants in making trouble at Xining, the Emperor dispatched banner commander Chu Zong to restrain them; when Chu arrived, Yunsi did not come out to receive him; an edict was transmitted rebuking him; he said: "The Emperor's rebukes of me are all justified—what more can I say?
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, learning that Yunsi indulged his household servants in making trouble at Xining, the Emperor dispatched banner commander Chu Zong to restrain them. When Chu arrived, Yunsi did not come out to receive him. An edict was transmitted rebuking him, and Yunsi said: "The Emperor's rebukes of me are all justified—what more can I say?

sentences.zh: 我行將出家離世！」

translations.literal: I am about to leave the world and become a monk!"
translations.idiomatic: I am about to leave the world and become a monk!"

sentences.zh: 楚宗以聞，上以允禟傲慢無人臣禮，手詔深責之，並牽連及允禩、允、允䄉私結黨援諸事。

translations.literal: Chu reported this; the Emperor, because Yunsi was arrogant and lacked the decorum of a subject, personally drafted a severe rebuke, and linked the matter to Yinsi, Yun, and Yun'e clandestinely forming factions and providing mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Chu reported this. The Emperor, finding Yunsi arrogant and lacking a subject's decorum, personally drafted a severe rebuke and linked the matter to Yinsi, Yinti, and Yun'e clandestinely forming factions and supporting one another.

sentences.zh: 七月，山烏雅圖等經平定毆諸生，請按律治罪，陝西人稱允禟九王，為上？

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Shan Wuyatu and others passed through Pingding and beat students; punishment according to law was requested; people in Shaanxi called Yunsi the Ninth Prince; the Emperor?
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Yunsi's guards Wuyatu and others passed through Pingding and beat students; punishment according to law was requested. People in Shaanxi called Yunsi the Ninth Prince, and the matter came to the Emperor's attention.

sentences.zh: 西巡撫伊都立奏劾允禟護所聞，手詔斥為無恥，遂奪允禟爵，撤所屬佐領，即西寧幽禁，並錄允禟左右用事者毛太、佟保等，撤還京師，授以官。

translations.literal: Provincial governor Yiduli of Xi memorialized impeaching Yunsi's guards upon hearing of it; the Emperor personally drafted a rebuke calling him shameless; Yunsi's rank was then stripped, his company commanders withdrawn; he was confined at Xining; Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others who wielded power at Yunsi's side were listed and recalled to the capital and given offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi governor Yiduli memorialized impeaching Yunsi after hearing of it. The Emperor personally drafted a rebuke calling him shameless, stripped Yunsi of his rank, withdrew his company commanders, and confined him at Xining. Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others who wielded power at Yunsi's side were listed, recalled to the capital, and given offices.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，九門捕役得毛太、佟保等寄允禟私書，以聞，上見書跡類西洋字，遣持問允禟子弘暘，弘暘言允禟所造字也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, runners of the Nine Gates obtained private letters Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others had sent Yunsi and reported them; the Emperor saw the script resembled Western letters and sent someone to ask Yunsi's son Hongyang; Hongyang said they were characters Yunsi had invented.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, runners of the Nine Gates obtained private letters that Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others had sent Yunsi and reported them. The Emperor saw that the script resembled Western letters and sent someone to ask Yunsi's son Hongyang, who said they were characters Yunsi had invented.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「從來造作隱語，防人察覺，惟敵國為然。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Throughout history, devising secret language to evade detection is something only enemy states do.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Throughout history, devising secret language to evade detection is something only enemy states do.

sentences.zh: 允禟在西寧，未嘗禁其書札往來，何至別造字體，暗藏密遞，不可令人以共見耶？

translations.literal: Yunsi was at Xining; his correspondence was never forbidden—why invent a separate script and secretly transmit hidden messages that cannot be openly seen together?
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi was at Xining and his correspondence was never forbidden—so why invent a separate script and secretly transmit messages that cannot be openly read?

sentences.zh: 允禟與弘暘書用朱筆，弘暘復書稱其父言為'旨'，皆僭妄非禮。

translations.literal: Yunsi's letters to Hongyang used vermilion ink; Hongyang's replies called his father's words 'edicts'—all presumptuous, reckless, and improper.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi's letters to Hongyang were written in vermilion ink, and Hongyang's replies called his father's words 'edicts'—all presumptuous, reckless, and improper.

sentences.zh: 允禟寄允䄉書言'事機已失'，其言尤駭人。」

translations.literal: Yunsi wrote to Yun'e saying 'the opportunity is already lost'—those words were especially alarming."
translations.idiomatic: Yunsi wrote to Yun'e saying 'the opportunity is already lost'—words especially alarming."

sentences.zh: 命嚴鞫毛太、佟保等。

translations.literal: He ordered Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others rigorously interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Mao Tai, Tong Bao, and others rigorously interrogated.

sentences.zh: 諸王大臣請治允禟罪，命革去黃帶子，削宗籍，逮還京，令胡什禮監以行。

translations.literal: The princes and senior ministers requested Yunsi be punished; he was ordered stripped of his yellow girdle and clan registration, arrested and brought back to the capital, with Hushili supervising the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and senior ministers asked that Yunsi be punished. He was stripped of his yellow girdle and clan registration, arrested, and brought back to the capital under Hushili's supervision.

sentences.zh: 五月，令允禟改名，又以所擬字樣姦巧，下諸王大臣議，改為塞？

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Yunsi was ordered to change his name; because the proposed characters were cunningly contrived, the matter was referred to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation; he was renamed Sai?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yunsi was ordered to change his name. Because the characters he proposed were cunningly contrived, the matter was referred to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation, and he was renamed Seshehei.

sentences.zh: 楚宗及侍思黑。

translations.literal: Chu Zong and attendant Sihei.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Zong and bodyguard Hushili supervised the journey.

sentences.zh: 六月，諸王大臣复劾允禟罪狀二十八事，請誅之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the princes and senior ministers again impeached Yunsi on twenty-eight counts and requested his execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the princes and senior ministers again impeached Yunsi on twenty-eight counts and asked that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 胡什禮監允禟至保定，命直隸總督李紱暫禁，觀其行止。

translations.literal: Hushili supervised Yunsi to Baoding; the Zhili governor Li Fu was ordered temporarily to detain him and observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Hushili supervised Yunsi as far as Baoding, where Zhili governor Li Fu was ordered temporarily to detain him and observe his conduct.

sentences.zh: 紱語胡什禮「當便宜行事」，胡什禮以聞，上命馳諭止之，紱奏無此語。

translations.literal: Li told Hushili, "When expedient, act on your own authority"; Hushili reported this; the Emperor dispatched urgent orders to stop it; Li memorialized that he had said no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: Li told Hushili, "When expedient, act on your own authority." Hushili reported this, and the Emperor dispatched urgent orders to stop it. Li then memorialized that he had said no such thing.

sentences.zh: 八月，紱奏允禟以腹疾卒於幽所。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Li memorialized that Yunsi had died of abdominal illness in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li memorialized that Yunsi had died of abdominal illness in confinement.

sentences.zh: 上聞胡什禮與楚宗中途械系允禟，旋釋去，胡什禮又，乃起流言也。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned that Hushili and Chu Zong had shackled Yunsi midway, then released him; Hushili again [—], and rumors arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor learned that Hushili and Chu Zong had shackled Yunsi en route and then released him. Hushili again [acted wrongly], and rumors spread.

sentences.zh: 乾？

translations.literal: Qian?
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign,

sentences.zh: 妄述紱語，命並逮治。

translations.literal: Falsely relating Li's words, they were ordered arrested and punished together.
translations.idiomatic: For falsely repeating Li's words, they were ordered arrested and punished together.

sentences.zh: 其後紱得罪，上猶責紱不以允禟死狀明白於隆間，復原名，還宗籍。

translations.literal: Later Li fell into disgrace; the Emperor still rebuked Li for not making Yunsi's death clearly known in Longjian; the original name was restored and clan registration returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li fell from favor, the Emperor still rebuked him for not reporting Yunsi's death clearly to the public, which gave rise to rumors. During the Qianlong reign Yunsi's original name was restored and his clan registration returned.

sentences.zh: 子弘晸，封不入八分輔國公，坐事奪爵。

translations.literal: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as fuguo gong without the eight privileges; for an offense his rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjing was enfeoffed as fuguo gong without the eight privileges, but later lost his rank for an offense.

sentences.zh: 輔國公允䄉，聖祖第十子。

translations.literal: Fuguo Gong Yun'e was the Holy Ancestor's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo Gong Yun'e was the Kangxi Emperor's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年十月，封敦郡王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as dun junwang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as Prince Dun.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，命辦理正黃旗滿洲、蒙古、漢軍三旗事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was ordered to manage the affairs of the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banners of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was ordered to manage the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banners of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 允䄉與允禟、允皆黨附允禩，為世宗所惡。

translations.literal: Yun'e, together with Yunsi and Yun, all attached themselves to Yinsi's faction and were hated by the Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'e, together with Yunsi and Yinti, all attached themselves to Yinsi's faction and were hated by the Yongzheng Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，澤卜尊丹巴胡土克圖詣京師，謁聖祖梓宮，俄病卒，上遣送靈龕還喀爾喀，命允䄉齎印冊賜奠。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 1, the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu came to the capital to pay respects at the Holy Ancestor's coffin; he soon fell ill and died; the Emperor ordered his spirit tablet sent back to Khalkha and ordered Yun'e to carry the seal and patent to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 the Jebtsundamba Khutuktu came to the capital to pay respects at the Kangxi Emperor's coffin, but soon fell ill and died. The Emperor ordered his spirit tablet sent back to Khalkha and ordered Yun'e to carry the seal and patent to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 允䄉託疾不行，旋稱有旨召還，居張家口。

translations.literal: Yun'e pleaded illness and did not go; soon he claimed an edict had recalled him and stayed at Zhangjiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'e pleaded illness and did not go. Soon he claimed an edict had recalled him and remained at Zhangjiakou.

sentences.zh: 复私行禳禱，疏文內連書「雍正新君」，為上所知，斥為不敬。

translations.literal: He again privately performed prayers and exorcisms; within the memorial text he repeatedly wrote "the new ruler Yongzheng"; when the Emperor learned of this he rebuked him for disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: He again privately performed prayers and exorcisms, and within the memorial text repeatedly wrote "the new ruler Yongzheng." When the Emperor learned of this he rebuked him for disrespect.

sentences.zh: 兵部劾奏，命允禩議其罪。

translations.literal: The Board of War impeached and memorialized; the Emperor ordered Yinsi to deliberate his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of War impeached and memorialized, and the Emperor ordered Yinsi to deliberate his guilt.

sentences.zh: 四月，奪爵，逮京師拘禁。

translations.literal: In the fourth month his rank was stripped; he was arrested and confined in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month his rank was stripped and he was arrested and confined in the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，高宗命釋之，封輔國公。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 2, the Gaozong ordered his release and enfeoffed him as fuguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 the Qianlong Emperor ordered his release and enfeoffed him as fuguo gong.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，詔用貝子品級祭葬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; an edict ordered funeral rites at beizi rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, and an edict ordered funeral rites at beizi rank.

sentences.zh: 履懿親王允祹，聖祖第十二子。

translations.literal: Prince Luyi Yuntao was the Holy Ancestor's twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Luyi Yuntao was the Kangxi Emperor's twelfth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年十月，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Kangxi 48 he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 自是有巡幸，輒從。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever there were inspection tours, he accompanied them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the Emperor went on inspection tours, he accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，孝惠章皇后崩，署內務府總管事務，大事將畢，乃罷。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, when Empress Xiaohuizhang died, he served as acting director-general of the Imperial Household Department; when the major rites were nearly complete, he was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year, when Empress Xiaohuizhang died, he served as acting director-general of the Imperial Household Department and was relieved once the major rites were nearly complete.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，辦理正白旗滿洲、蒙古、漢軍三旗事。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he managed the affairs of the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banners of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he managed the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Banners of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 六十年，上以御極六十年，遣允祹祭盛京三陵。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, because the Emperor had reigned sixty years, he dispatched Yuntao to offer sacrifices at the three tombs of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year, because the Emperor had reigned sixty years, he dispatched Yuntao to offer sacrifices at the three tombs of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，授鑲黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he was appointed Manchu banner commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he was appointed Manchu banner commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，進封履郡王。

translations.literal: When the Shizong acceded, Yuntao was promoted to luyi junwang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor acceded, Yuntao was promoted to Prince Luyi.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，宗人府劾允祹治事不能敬謹，請奪爵，命在固山貝子上行走。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 2, the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yuntao for inability to manage affairs with reverent care and requested stripping his rank; he was ordered to walk in rank below gushan beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yuntao for failing to manage affairs with reverent care and asked that his rank be stripped. He was ordered to walk in rank below gushan beizi.

sentences.zh: 二月，因聖祖配享儀注及封妃金冊遺漏舛錯，降鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the second month, because of omissions and errors in the rites for the Holy Ancestor's spirit tablet and the golden patent for ennobling a consort, he was demoted to zhenguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, because of omissions and errors in the rites for the Kangxi Emperor's spirit tablet and the golden patent for ennobling a consort, he was demoted to zhenguo gong.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，复封郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year his rank as junwang was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year his rank as junwang was restored.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進封履親王。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong acceded, Yuntao was promoted to luyi qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor acceded, Yuntao was promoted to Prince Luyi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年七月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Qianlong 28 he died; a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianlong 28 he died and was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子弘昆，先卒，用世子例殯葬，餘子皆未封。

translations.literal: His son Hongkun died first; he was buried with the rites for an heir; the remaining sons were none enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongkun died first and was buried with the rites for an heir; none of the remaining sons were enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 高宗命以皇四子永為允祹後，襲郡王。

translations.literal: The Gaozong ordered the Emperor's fourth son Yong to be made Yuntao's heir and to inherit the junwang rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor ordered the Emperor's fourth son Yongqi to be made Yuntao's heir and to inherit the junwang rank.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，薨，諡曰端。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died; posthumous title Duan was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he died and was granted the posthumous title Duan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，追封親王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he was posthumously enfeoffed as qinwang.

sentences.zh: 子綿惠，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Mianhui inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mianhui inherited as beile.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，薨，追封郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as junwang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as junwang.

sentences.zh: 以成郡王綿懃子奕綸為後，襲貝子，進貝勒。

translations.literal: Yicheng Junwang Mianqin's son Yilun was made heir, inherited as beizi, and was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng Junwang Mianqin's son Yilun was made heir, inherited as beizi, and was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants declined in rank by the usual rule, with zhenguo gong inherited in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants declined in rank by the usual rule, with zhenguo gong inherited in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十二年，高宗南巡，還蹕次涿州，有僧攜童子迎駕，自言永庶子，為側室福晉王氏所棄，僧育以長。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 42, when the Gaozong toured the south and returned, halting at Zhuozhou, a monk brought a boy to greet the imperial procession, saying he was Yong's shuzi, abandoned by a secondary consort surnamed Wang, and raised by the monk.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 42, when the Qianlong Emperor toured the south and returned, halting at Zhuozhou, a monk brought a boy to greet the imperial procession, saying he was Yong's shuzi, abandoned by a secondary consort surnamed Wang and raised by the monk.

sentences.zh: 上問永嫡福晉伊爾根覺羅氏，言永子以痘殤。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Yong's primary consort Irgen Gioro; she said Yong's son had died of smallpox.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Yong's primary consort of the Irgen Gioro clan; she said Yong's son had died of smallpox.

sentences.zh: 乃令入都，命軍機大臣詰之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the boy brought to the capital and commanded the Grand Council ministers to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the boy brought to the capital and commanded the Grand Council ministers to interrogate him.

sentences.zh: 童子端坐名諸大臣，諸大臣不敢決。

translations.literal: The boy sat upright and named the senior ministers; the senior ministers did not dare decide.
translations.idiomatic: The boy sat upright and named the senior ministers one by one, but the senior ministers did not dare decide.

sentences.zh: 軍機章京保成直前批其頰，叱之，童子乃自承劉氏子，僧教為妄語。

translations.literal: Grand Council clerk Bao Cheng stepped forward and struck him on the cheek, rebuking him; the boy then confessed of himself that he was a Liu clansman's son, and that the monk had taught him to speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Council clerk Bao Cheng stepped forward, struck the boy on the cheek, and rebuked him; the boy then confessed on his own that he was the son of a man surnamed Liu and that the monk had coached him to lie.

sentences.zh: 斬僧，戍童子伊犁，仍自稱皇孫，所為多不法。

translations.literal: The monk was beheaded; the boy was banished to Yili. He still called himself the Emperor's grandson, and his conduct was largely unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: The monk was executed and the boy was exiled to Yili. Even so, he continued to call himself the Emperor's grandson, and much of what he did was unlawful.

sentences.zh: 上命改戍黑龍江，道庫倫，庫倫辦事大臣松筠責其不法，縛出，絞殺之，高宗嘉其明決。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that his exile be changed to Heilongjiang. Passing through Kulun, Kulun Commissioner Songyun rebuked him for unlawful conduct, bound him, took him out, and had him strangled to death; Gaozong praised his clear and resolute action.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered that his place of exile be changed to Heilongjiang. When he passed through Kulun, the Kulun Commissioner Songyun censured him for unlawful conduct, had him bound and taken out, and had him strangled. The Qianlong Emperor commended Songyun for his clear and resolute handling of the matter.

sentences.zh: 怡賢親王允祥，聖祖第十三子。

translations.literal: Prince Yi Xian Yinxiang was the Kangxi Emperor's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi the Worthy, Yinxiang, was the thirteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十七年，從上謁陵。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 37 he accompanied the Emperor in paying respects at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 37 he accompanied the Emperor on a visit to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 自是有巡幸，輒從。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever there was an imperial tour, he always accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the Emperor went on tour, he went with him.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，封為怡親王。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year the Shizong ascended the throne and enfeoffed him as Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi, when the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 尋命總理戶部三庫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to take overall charge of the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to take overall charge of the Board of Revenue's three treasuries.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命總理戶部。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 1 he was ordered to take overall charge of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was ordered to take overall charge of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十一月，諭：「怡親王於皇考時敬謹廉潔，家計空乏，舉國皆知。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict said: 'During our late father's reign, Prince Yi was reverent, careful, honest, and clean-handed; his household finances were empty and strained, and the whole realm knew it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Emperor issued an edict: 'During our late father's reign, Prince Yi was reverent, careful, honest, and incorruptible; his household was known throughout the realm to be poor.

sentences.zh: 朕御極以來，一心翊戴，克盡臣弟之道。

translations.literal: Since We ascended the throne, he has wholeheartedly supported Us and fully fulfilled the way of a subject and younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Since We took the throne, he has wholeheartedly supported Us and fully lived up to his duty as both subject and younger brother.

sentences.zh: 從前兄弟分封，各得錢糧二十三萬兩，朕援此例賜之，奏辭不已，宣諭再四，僅受十三萬；

translations.literal: When Our brothers were enfeoffed in former times, each received 230,000 taels in stipends and grain. We followed this precedent in granting it to him, but in memorial after memorial he declined; though We announced and instructed him repeatedly, he accepted only 130,000;
translations.idiomatic: When Our brothers were enfeoffed in earlier times, each received 230,000 taels in money and grain. We followed that precedent in making the grant, but he declined again and again in memorials; though We announced and instructed him repeatedly, he accepted only 130,000 taels;

sentences.zh: 复援裕親王例，令支官物六年，王又固辭。

translations.literal: We again cited the precedent of Prince Yu and ordered that official goods be supplied for six years; the prince again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: We again cited the precedent set for Prince Yu and ordered that official goods be supplied for six years, but the prince once more firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 今不允所請，既不可；

translations.literal: Now, if We do not grant what he asks, that too is impossible;
translations.idiomatic: Now, if We refuse what he asks, that cannot be done either;

sentences.zh: 允其請，而實心為國之懿親，轉不得與諸弟兄比，朕心不安。」

translations.literal: yet if We grant his request, this worthy kinsman who truly serves the state with all his heart would in turn be unable to compare with Our other brothers, and Our heart is uneasy.'
translations.idiomatic: yet if We grant his request, this worthy kinsman who truly serves the state with all his heart would then be treated no better than Our other brothers, and that weighs on Our mind.'

sentences.zh: 下諸王大臣議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for deliberation by the princes and senior ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the princes and senior ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 既，仍允王請，命王所兼管佐領俱為王一等一員、二等四員、三等十二員，豹尾槍二、長桿刀二，每佐領增親軍二名？

translations.literal: Afterward, the prince's request was still granted. It was ordered that the company commanders under the prince's concurrent charge all become the prince's: one officer of the first rank, four of the second rank, and twelve of the third rank, two leopard-tail muskets and two long-shafted sabers, and two added personal guards in each company.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation, the prince's request was still granted. The company commanders under his concurrent charge were all assigned to him, with one first-rank officer, four second-rank officers, and twelve third-rank officers, two leopard-tail muskets and two long-shafted sabers, and two additional personal guards in each company.

sentences.zh: 屬，加護。

translations.literal: retainers, with guards added.
translations.idiomatic: They were made his retainers, with an added guard detachment.

sentences.zh: 二年，允祥請除加色、加平諸弊，並增設三庫主事、庫大使，從之。

translations.literal: In the second year Yinxiang requested the removal of abuses such as added surcharges and added balance fees, and the addition of chief clerks and treasury wardens for the three treasuries; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yinxiang requested the elimination of abuses such as added surcharges and added balance fees, and the creation of chief clerk and treasury warden posts for the three treasuries; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，三年服滿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, the three-year mourning period was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, the three-year mourning period came to an end.

sentences.zh: 以王總理事務謹慎忠誠，從優議敘，復加封郡王，任王於諸子？

translations.literal: Because the prince had managed affairs with prudence and loyalty, he was given a special merit commendation, again enfeoffed as a junwang, and entrusted to choose among his sons
translations.idiomatic: Because the prince had managed affairs with prudence and loyalty, he was given a special merit commendation, enfeoffed again as a junwang, and entrusted to choose among his sons

sentences.zh: 中指封。

translations.literal: for the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: for the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 八月，加俸銀萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month his salary stipend was increased by ten thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month his salary stipend was increased by ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 京畿被水，命往勘。

translations.literal: The capital region suffered flooding; he was ordered to go and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region was inundated, he was ordered to go and inspect the damage.

sentences.zh: 十二月，令總理京畿水利。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was ordered to take overall charge of water control in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was ordered to take overall charge of waterworks in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「直隸河與汶河合流東下。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: 'The rivers of Zhili and the Wen River join and flow eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: 'The Wei River of Zhili and the Wen River join and flow eastward.

sentences.zh: 滄、景以下，春？

translations.literal: Below Cangzhou and Jingzhou, in spring
translations.idiomatic: Below Cangzhou and Jingzhou, in spring the rivers are largely shallow and obstructed;

sentences.zh: 河、淀河、子牙河、永定河皆匯於天津大直沽入海，河？

translations.literal: the river, the Dian River, the Ziya River, and the Yongding River all converge at Dazhigu in Tianjin to enter the sea; the rivers
translations.idiomatic: the Wei River, the Dian River, the Ziya River, and the Yongding River all converge at Dazhigu in Tianjin and enter the sea; the rivers

sentences.zh: 多淺阻，伏秋暴漲，不免潰溢。

translations.literal: are largely shallow and obstructed; during the dog days and autumn they surge violently, inevitably bursting their banks.
translations.idiomatic: are largely shallow and obstructed, and during the dog days and autumn they surge violently, inevitably bursting their banks.

sentences.zh: 請將滄州磚河、青縣興濟河故道疏濬，築減水壩，以洩之漲；

translations.literal: He requested that the old channels of the Brick River at Cangzhou and the Xingji River at Qing County be dredged and cleared, and overflow dams built to discharge the surging waters;
translations.idiomatic: He requested that the old channels of Cangzhou's Brick River and Qing County's Xingji River be dredged and cleared, and that overflow dams be built to discharge the surging waters of the Wei River;

sentences.zh: 並於白塘口入海處開直河，使磚河、興濟河同歸白塘出海；

translations.literal: and that at the place where the waters enter the sea at Baitang Mouth a straight channel be opened, so that the Brick River and the Xingji River may together return to the sea through Baitang;
translations.idiomatic: and that a straight channel be opened at Baitang Mouth where the rivers enter the sea, so that the Brick River and the Xingji River may both discharge through Baitang;

sentences.zh: 又濬東、西二淀，多開引河，使脈絡相通，溝澮四達；

translations.literal: He also proposed dredging the eastern and western marshes, opening many diversion channels so that their network would connect and the ditches reach in all directions;
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed dredging the eastern and western marshes, opening many diversion channels so that their waterways would connect and the ditches reach in all directions;

sentences.zh: 仍疏趙北、苑家二口以防衝決。

translations.literal: and still clearing the two mouths at Zhaobei and Yuanjia to guard against breach and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: and clearing the two outlets at Zhaobei and Yuanjia to guard against breaches.

sentences.zh: 子牙河為滹沱及漳水下流，其下有清河、夾河、月河同趨於淀，宜開決分注，緩其奔放之勢。

translations.literal: The Ziya River is the lower course of the Hutuo and Zhang Rivers; below it the Qing River, Jia River, and Yue River all rush together toward the marshes. It is fitting to open breaches and divide the flow to slow their rushing force.
translations.idiomatic: The Ziya River is the lower course of the Hutuo and Zhang Rivers; below it the Qing, Jia, and Yue Rivers all rush together toward the marshes. He proposed opening breaches to divide the flow and slow their force.

sentences.zh: 永定河故道已湮，應自柳義水所歸，應逐年疏濬，使濁水不能為患？

translations.literal: The old channel of the Yongding River has silted up. From Liuyi it should be where the waters gather; it should be dredged year by year so that muddy water cannot become a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The old channel of the Yongding River has silted up. From the Liuyi outlet the waters should be led to where they gather; the channel should be dredged year by year so that muddy water cannot become a hazard.

sentences.zh: 口引之稍北，繞王慶坨東北入淀，至三角淀，為又請於京東灤、薊、天津，京南文、霸、任丘、新、雄諸州縣設營田專官，募農耕種。」

translations.literal: From the mouth lead it slightly north, circling northeast of Wangqingtuo to enter the marshes as far as Sanjiao Marsh, where all waters gather; he also requested that special officials for garrison-farm colonies be established in the prefectures and counties of Luan, Ji, and Tianjin east of the capital, and Wen'an, Ba, Renqiu, Xin, and Xiong south of the capital, to recruit farmers for cultivation.'
translations.idiomatic: From the outlet it should be led slightly north, circling northeast of Wangqingtuo to enter the marshes as far as Sanjiao Marsh, where all the waters gather. He also requested special officials for garrison-farm colonies in Luan, Ji, and Tianjin east of the capital and Wen'an, Ba, Renqiu, Xin, and Xiong south of the capital, to recruit farmers for cultivation.'

sentences.zh: 四年二月，疏言直隸興修水利，請分諸河為四局，下吏、工諸部議，議以南運河與臧家橋以下之子牙河、苑家口以東之淀河為一局，令天津道領之；

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, in a memorial on waterworks in Zhili he requested that the rivers be divided into four bureaus. The matter was sent down to the Boards of Civil Appointments and Works for deliberation. They proposed that the Southern Grand Canal together with the Ziya River below Zangjia Bridge and the Dian River east of Yuanjia Mouth form one bureau, to be led by the Tianjin intendant;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, in a memorial on waterworks in Zhili he requested that the rivers be divided into four bureaus. The matter was referred to the Boards of Civil Appointments and Works. They proposed that the Southern Grand Canal together with the Ziya River below Zangjia Bridge and the Dian River east of Yuanjia Mouth form one bureau under the Tianjin intendant;

sentences.zh: 苑家口以西各淀池及畿南諸河為一局，以大名道改清河道領之；

translations.literal: the various marshes west of Yuanjia Mouth and the rivers south of the capital region as one bureau, to be led by the Qinghe intendant converted from the Daming intendant;
translations.idiomatic: the various marshes west of Yuanjia Mouth and the rivers south of the capital region as one bureau under the Qinghe intendant, converted from the Daming intendant;

sentences.zh: 永定河為一局，以永定分司改道領之；

translations.literal: the Yongding River as one bureau, to be led by the Yongding sub-commissioner converted to an intendant;
translations.idiomatic: the Yongding River as one bureau under the Yongding sub-commissioner converted to an intendant;

sentences.zh: 北運河為一局，撤分司以通永道領之：分隸專官管轄。

translations.literal: the Northern Grand Canal as one bureau, with the sub-commissioner abolished and the Tongyong intendant placed in charge: each placed under the jurisdiction of a dedicated official.
translations.idiomatic: and the Northern Grand Canal as one bureau, with the sub-commissioner abolished and the Tongyong intendant placed in charge—each under the jurisdiction of a dedicated official.

sentences.zh: 尋又命分設京東、京西水利營田使各一。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again ordered to establish separately one commissioner each for water control and garrison farms east and west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward separate commissioners for water control and garrison farms were established east and west of the capital, one in each region.

sentences.zh: 三月，疏陳京東水利諸事。

translations.literal: In the third month he memorialized setting forth the various matters of water control east of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he memorialized on the various water-control projects east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，疏陳畿輔西南水利諸事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he memorialized setting forth the various matters of water control in the southwest of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he memorialized on the various water-control projects in the southwest of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were sent down to the boards for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All were referred to the boards for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 七月，賜御書「忠敬誠直勤慎廉明」榜，諭曰：「怡親王事朕，克殫忠誠，職掌有九，而公爾忘私，視國如家，朕深知王德，覺此八字無一毫過量之詞。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was granted an imperial inscription reading 'Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, careful, honest, and clear-sighted,' with an edict saying: 'Prince Yi serves Us and fully exhausts his loyalty and sincerity. He holds nine offices, yet treats public duty as private interest forgotten and regards the state as his own household. We know the prince's virtue deeply and feel that these eight characters contain not a trace of excessive praise.
