translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was granted an imperial inscription reading 'Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, careful, honest, and clear-sighted,' with an edict saying: 'Prince Yi serves Us with complete loyalty and sincerity. He holds nine offices, yet sets aside private interest for the public good and treats the state as his own household. We know the prince's character well and feel that these eight words contain not a trace of excessive praise.

sentences.zh: 在朝諸臣，於'忠勤慎明'尚多有之，若'敬誠直廉'，則未能輕許。

translations.literal: Among the ministers at court, many still possess 'loyalty, diligence, care, and clarity,' but as for 'reverence, sincerity, uprightness, and honesty,' one cannot lightly grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ministers at court, many may still claim 'loyalty, diligence, care, and clarity,' but as for 'reverence, sincerity, uprightness, and honesty,' those cannot be lightly bestowed.

sentences.zh: 期咸砥礪，以副朕望。」

translations.literal: We expect all to polish themselves to meet Our hopes.'
translations.idiomatic: We expect all of you to refine yourselves accordingly.'

sentences.zh: 七年六月，命辦理西北兩路軍​​機。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year he was ordered to manage military affairs on the northwestern two routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year he was ordered to manage military affairs on the northwestern two routes.

sentences.zh: 十月，命增儀仗一倍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was ordered to increase his ceremonial guard by one full set.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was ordered to double his ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王有疾。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the prince fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the prince fell ill.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，疾篤，上親臨視，及至，王已薨，上悲慟，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year his illness became grave. The Emperor went in person to visit him, but when he arrived the prince had already died. The Emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year his illness became grave. The Emperor went in person to see him, but when he arrived the prince had already died. The Emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for three days.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上親臨奠，諭：「怡親王薨逝，中心悲慟，飲食無味，寢臥不安。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor went in person to offer sacrifice and said: 'Prince Yi has died. Our heart is deeply grieved; food has no taste and sleep brings no rest.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor went in person to offer sacrifice and said: 'Prince Yi has died. Our heart is stricken with grief; food has no taste and sleep brings no rest.

sentences.zh: 王事朕八年如一日，自古無此公忠體國之賢王，朕待王亦宜在常例之外。

translations.literal: The prince served Us for eight years as if it were one day. Since antiquity there has never been such a worthy prince who served the public with loyalty and embodied the state. Our treatment of the prince should also be outside the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: The prince served Us for eight years as faithfully as if it were a single day. Never in history has there been such a worthy prince who served the public with loyalty and embodied the interests of the state. Our treatment of him should likewise go beyond ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 今朕素服一月，諸臣常服，宴會俱不必行。」

translations.literal: Now We shall wear plain mourning for one month; the ministers shall wear ordinary dress, and banquets need not be held.'
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth We shall wear plain mourning for one month; the ministers shall wear ordinary dress, and no banquets need be held.'

sentences.zh: 越日，复諭舉怡親王功德，命復其名上一字為「胤」，配享太廟，諡曰賢，並以「忠敬誠直勤慎廉明」八字加於諡上。

translations.literal: The following day he again issued an edict recounting Prince Yi's merits and virtues, ordering that the first character of his name be restored as 'Yin,' that he be granted posthumous sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, given the posthumous title Xian, and that the eight characters 'Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, careful, honest, and clear-sighted' be added above the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he issued another edict recounting Prince Yi's merits and virtues, ordering that the first character of his name be restored as 'Yin,' that he be granted posthumous sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, given the posthumous title Xian, and that the eight words 'Loyal, reverent, sincere, upright, diligent, careful, honest, and clear-sighted' be added to his posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 白家甿等十三村民請建祠，允之。

translations.literal: Villagers from thirteen villages including Baijiameng requested that a shrine be built; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers from thirteen villages including Baijiameng requested that a shrine be built in his honor; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 撥官地三十餘頃為祭田，免租賦。

translations.literal: More than thirty qing of official land were allocated as sacrificial fields, exempt from rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty qing of official land were set aside as sacrificial fields, exempt from rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 命更定園寢之制，視常例有加。

translations.literal: He ordered that the regulations for the garden tomb be revised, with additions beyond the usual rule.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that the regulations for the garden tomb be revised, with additions beyond ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 又命未殯，月賜祭；

translations.literal: He also ordered that before interment, sacrificial offerings be granted monthly;
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that before interment, sacrificial offerings be granted each month;

sentences.zh: 小祥及殯，視大祭禮賜祭；

translations.literal: at the xiaoxiang observance and at interment, offerings be granted according to the rites of a major sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: at the xiaoxiang observance and at interment, offerings be granted according to the rites of a major state sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 三年後，歲賜祭。

translations.literal: after three years, offerings be granted annually.
translations.idiomatic: and after three years, offerings be granted annually.

sentences.zh: 皆特恩，不為例。

translations.literal: All were special favors and were not to become precedent.
translations.idiomatic: All were special favors and were not to become precedent.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，祀盛京賢王祠。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he was sacrificed at the Shrine of Worthy Princes in Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he was enshrined at the Shrine of Worthy Princes in Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 命王爵世襲。

translations.literal: The prince's rank was ordered to pass in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: The princely title was ordered to pass in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 子弘曉，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hongxiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongxiao succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年，薨，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 43 he died; his posthumous title was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 43 he died and was given the posthumous title Xi.

sentences.zh: 子永瑯，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yonglang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yonglang succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，薨，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In Jiaqing 4 he died; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he died and was given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 孫奕勳，襲。

translations.literal: His grandson Yixun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yixun succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died and was given the posthumous title Ke.

sentences.zh: 子載坊，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zaifang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zaifang succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 明年，薨。

translations.literal: The following year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died.

sentences.zh: 弟載垣，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zaichuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zaichuan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 事宣宗，命在御大臣。

translations.literal: Serving the Daoguang Emperor, he was ordered to serve as a Grand Minister in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the Daoguang Emperor, he was appointed a Grand Minister in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，賜紫禁城內肩？

translations.literal: In Xianfeng 8 he was granted use of a sedan chair within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 8 he was granted the privilege of riding in a sedan chair within the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 前大臣行走，受顧命。

translations.literal: He served as a Grand Minister in Attendance and received the dying imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Grand Minister in Attendance and received the Emperor's deathbed command.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，歷左宗正、宗令、領侍輿。

translations.literal: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, Zaichuan successively held the posts of Left Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Minister in charge of the Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne, he successively served as Left Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Minister in charge of the Imperial Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 載垣與鄭王端華及端華弟肅順皆為上所倚，相結，權勢日張。

translations.literal: Zaichuan, Prince Zheng Duanhua, and Duanhua's younger brother Sushun were all relied upon by the Emperor. They formed a faction, and their power grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Zaichuan, Prince Zheng Duanhua, and Duanhua's younger brother Sushun were all men on whom the Emperor relied. They formed a faction, and their power grew daily.

sentences.zh: 九年，命赴天津察視海防。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to go to Tianjin to inspect coastal defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was ordered to go to Tianjin to inspect the coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，萬壽節，賜杏黃色端罩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, on the Emperor's birthday, he was granted an apricot-yellow formal surcoat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, on the Emperor's birthday, he was granted an apricot-yellow formal surcoat.

sentences.zh: 七月，英吉利、法蘭西兩國兵至天津，命與兵部尚書穆廕以欽差大臣赴通州與英人議和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the armies of England and France reached Tianjin. He was ordered, together with Minister of War Muyin, to go as Imperial Commissioner to Tongzhou to negotiate peace with the English.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the armies of England and France reached Tianjin. He was ordered, together with Minister of War Muyin, to go as Imperial Commissioner to Tongzhou to negotiate peace with the British.

sentences.zh: 時大學士桂良已於天津定議，上許英使額爾金至通州簽約，英使額爾金請入京師親遞國書，不許。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Secretary Guiliang had already settled terms at Tianjin. The Emperor permitted the English envoy Elgin to come to Tongzhou to sign the treaty, but when Elgin requested to enter the capital to deliver the letter of credence in person, this was refused.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Secretary Guiliang had already settled terms at Tianjin. The Emperor permitted the British envoy Elgin to come to Tongzhou to sign the treaty, but when Elgin requested to enter the capital to deliver the letter of credence in person, the request was refused.

sentences.zh: 兵復進，上以和議未成，罷載垣欽差大臣。

translations.literal: The armies advanced again. Because the peace talks had not succeeded, the Emperor removed Zaichuan from his post as Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The armies advanced again. Because the peace talks had failed, the Emperor removed Zaichuan from his post as Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，扈上幸熱河。

translations.literal: Before long he accompanied the Emperor on a visit to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he accompanied the Emperor on the flight to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 及和議定，？

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was settled,
translations.idiomatic: When the peace agreement was settled,

sentences.zh: 臣請還京師，上猶豫未決。

translations.literal: the ministers requested return to the capital; the Emperor hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: the ministers requested a return to the capital, but the Emperor hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，文宗崩，穆宗即位，載垣等受遺詔輔政，與端華、景壽、肅順及軍機大臣穆廕、匡源、杜翰、焦祐瀛稱「贊襄政務王大臣」，擅政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year the Xianfeng Emperor died and the Tongzhi Emperor ascended the throne. Zaichuan and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government. Together with Duanhua, Jingshou, Sushun, and the Grand Council ministers Muyin, Kuang Yuan, Du Han, and Jiao Youying they styled themselves 'Princes and Ministers Assisting in Government' and monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year the Xianfeng Emperor died and the Tongzhi Emperor ascended the throne. Zaichuan and others received the testamentary edict to assist in government. Together with Duanhua, Jingshou, Sushun, and the Grand Council ministers Muyin, Kuang Yuan, Du Han, and Jiao Youying they styled themselves 'Princes and Ministers Assisting in Government' and monopolized power.

sentences.zh: 九月，上奉文宗喪還京師，詔罪狀載垣等，奪爵職，下王大臣按治，議殊死，賜自盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor returned to the capital bearing the Xianfeng Emperor's coffin. An edict set forth the crimes of Zaichuan and the others, stripped them of rank and office, and sent them down to the princes and senior ministers for investigation. Death by the severest penalty was proposed, and they were granted permission to take their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Emperor returned to the capital with the Xianfeng Emperor's coffin. An edict set forth the crimes of Zaichuan and the others, stripped them of rank and office, and referred them to the princes and senior ministers for investigation. Death by the severest penalty was proposed, and they were granted permission to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 事詳肅順傳。

translations.literal: The affair is detailed in the biography of Sushun.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recounted in detail in the biography of Sushun.

sentences.zh: 爵降為不入八分輔國公，並命不得以其子孫及親兄弟子承襲。

translations.literal: The title was reduced to Junior Guardian of the State without the Eight Privileges, and it was ordered that neither his descendants nor the sons of his close brothers might succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The title was reduced to Junior Guardian of the State without the Eight Privileges, and it was ordered that neither his descendants nor the sons of his close brothers might succeed to it.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以莊親王允祿四世孫載泰襲輔國公，收府第敕書。

translations.literal: In Tongzhi 1, Zaitai, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Zhuang Yunlu, succeeded to the title of Junior Guardian of the State, and the princely residence and patent of enfeoffment were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 1, Zaitai, fourth-generation descendant of Prince Zhuang Yunlu, succeeded to the title of Junior Guardian of the State, and the princely residence and patent of enfeoffment were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，師克江寧，推恩還王爵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, when the army captured Jiangning, favor was extended and the princely rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, when the army captured Jiangning, an act of grace restored the princely rank.

sentences.zh: 九月，以寧郡王弘？

translations.literal: In the ninth month, using Prince Ning Junwang Hong Jiao's
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Prince Ning Junwang Hong Jiao's

sentences.zh: 四世孫鎮國公載敦襲怡親王，還敕書。

translations.literal: succeeded to the title of Prince Yi, and the patent of enfeoffment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: succeeded to the title of Prince Yi, and the patent of enfeoffment was returned.

sentences.zh: 光緒十六年，薨，諡，奪爵，以先薨免罪。

translations.literal: In Guangxu 16 he died; posthumous title; rank stripped; exempted from punishment because he had already died.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 16 Zaidun died and received the posthumous title Duan.

sentences.zh: 弟之？

translations.literal: The posthumous title was styled Duan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Duan.

sentences.zh: 曰端。

translations.literal: styled Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Styled Duan.

sentences.zh: 子溥靜，嗣。

translations.literal: His son Pujing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pujing succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 二十六年八月，薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, eighth month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, eighth month, he died.

sentences.zh: 九月，坐縱芘拳匪啟子毓麒，襲。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for condoning and shielding the Boxers and provoking conflict, the title was forfeited; as he had already died, punishment was waived. His younger brother's son Yuqi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, for sheltering and abetting the Boxers and thus provoking hostilities, his princely title was stripped away; because he had already died, he was spared further punishment. His younger brother's son Yuqi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 寧良郡王弘晈，允祥第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Ning the Good Hong Jiao was Yinxiang's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning the Good, Hong Jiao, was the fourth son of Prince Yi the Worthy, Yinxiang.

sentences.zh: 世宗褒允祥功，加封郡王，任王於諸子中指封，允祥固辭不敢承。

translations.literal: The Shizong praised Yinxiang's merit, added a junwang enfeoffment, and entrusted the prince to choose among his sons for the grant; Yinxiang firmly declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor praised Yinxiang's service, added a junwang enfeoffment, and entrusted him to designate one of his sons for the grant; Yinxiang firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 及允祥薨，世宗乃封弘？

translations.literal: When Yinxiang died, the Shizong then enfeoffed Hong Jiao
translations.idiomatic: After Yinxiang died, the Yongzheng Emperor enfeoffed Hong Jiao

sentences.zh: 寧郡王，世襲。

translations.literal: as Prince Ning, with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: as Prince Ning, with hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十九年八月，薨，諡曰良。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Qianlong, eighth month, he died; posthumous title Liang was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Qianlong, eighth month, he died and was given the posthumous title Liang.

sentences.zh: 子永福，仍循例襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yongfu still succeeded as beile according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongfu succeeded as beile in the usual manner.

sentences.zh: 四十七年九月，薨，諡恭恪。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, ninth month, he died; posthumous title Gongke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year, ninth month, he died and was given the posthumous title Gongke.

sentences.zh: 子綿譽，仍襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Mianyu still succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mianyu succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were demoted by successive degrees, with hereditary succession at the rank of gengguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants were demoted by successive degrees, and the line continued at the rank of gengguo gong.

sentences.zh: 載敦紹封怡親王，即以載泰襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: When Zaidun was restored as Prince Yi, Zaitai was at once made to succeed as gengguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zaidun was restored to the title of Prince Yi, Zaitai succeeded as gengguo gong.

sentences.zh: 允祥諸子：弘昌，初封貝子，進貝勒，坐事奪爵；

translations.literal: Yinxiang's sons: Hongchang, initially enfeoffed beizi, promoted to beile, convicted of an offense and stripped of his title;
translations.idiomatic: Yinxiang's sons included Hongchang, who was first enfeoffed as beizi and then promoted to beile, but was later convicted of an offense and deprived of his rank;

sentences.zh: 弘暾，未封早世，聘於富察氏，未婚守志，世宗愍之，命視貝勒例殯葬；

translations.literal: Hongdun, who died young before enfeoffment, was betrothed to a woman of the Fuca clan; though unmarried, she kept her chastity; the Shizong commiserated with her and ordered burial according to the beile precedent;
translations.idiomatic: Hongdun died young before receiving a title. Betrothed to a woman of the Fuca clan, she remained faithful though never married; the Yongzheng Emperor took pity on her and ordered that he be buried according to beile precedent;

sentences.zh: 弘昑，亦用其例。

translations.literal: Hongqin also received the same precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Hongqin was treated by the same precedent.

sentences.zh: 恂勤郡王允禵，聖祖第十四子。

translations.literal: Prince Xun the Diligent Yunti was the Kangxi Emperor's fourteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xun the Diligent, Yunti, was the fourteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 五十年，從上幸塞外。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he accompanied the Emperor on a tour beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he accompanied the Emperor on a tour beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 自是輒從。

translations.literal: From then on he always followed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always accompanied the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，賜銀四千兩。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he was granted four thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，命為撫遠大將軍，討策妄阿喇布坦。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief for Pacifying the West to attack Tsewang Araptan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief for Pacifying the West to campaign against Tsewang Araptan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，師行，上御太和殿授印，命用正黃旗纛。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army marched; the Emperor presided at the Hall of Supreme Harmony to confer the seal and ordered the use of the Plain Yellow Banner standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army set out. The Emperor presided at the Hall of Supreme Harmony to confer the seal and ordered the use of the Plain Yellow Banner standard.

sentences.zh: 五十八年四月，劾吏部侍郎色爾圖督兵餉失職，都統胡錫圖索詐騷擾，治其罪。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifty-eighth year he impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Se'ertu for mismanaging military supplies, and Commander Huxitu for extortion and harassment; they were punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifty-eighth year he impeached Vice Minister of Personnel Se'ertu for mismanaging military supplies and Commander Huxitu for extortion and harassment; both were punished.

sentences.zh: 都統延信疏稱：「準噶爾與青海聯姻婭，大將軍領兵出口，必有諜告準酋者，不若暫緩前進。」

translations.literal: Commander Yanxin memorialized: "The Dzungars are allied by marriage with Qinghai. When the Commander-in-Chief leads troops beyond the border, spies will surely inform the Dzungar chief; it would be better to halt the advance for the time being."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yanxin memorialized: "The Dzungars are allied by marriage with Qinghai. When the Commander-in-Chief leads troops beyond the border, spies will surely inform the Dzungar chief; it would be better to halt the advance for the time being."

sentences.zh: 上命駐西寧。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered a garrison at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the army to garrison at Xining.

sentences.zh: 五十九年正月，允禵移軍穆魯斯烏蘇，遣平逆將軍延信率師入西藏，令宗查布防西寧，訥爾素防古木。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifty-ninth year Yunti moved his army to Murusi Wusu, sent Pacifying General Yanxin to lead troops into Tibet, ordered Zongcha to defend Xining, and Naersu to defend Gumu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifty-ninth year Yunti moved his army to Murusi Wusu, dispatched Pacifying General Yanxin to lead troops into Tibet, ordered Zongcha to defend Xining, and Naersu to defend Gumu.

sentences.zh: 時別立新胡必爾汗，遣兵送之入藏。

translations.literal: At the time a new Qoshot Khan was installed separately, and troops were sent to escort him into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a new Qoshot Khan was installed separately, and troops were sent to escort him into Tibet.

sentences.zh: 十月，延信擊敗準噶爾將策零敦多卜等於卜克河諸地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yanxin defeated the Dzungar generals Tsewang Donjub and others at various places along the Bukha River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yanxin defeated the Dzungar generals Tsewang Donjub and others at various places along the Bukha River.

sentences.zh: 六十年五月，允禵率師駐甘州，進萬？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixtieth year Yunti led his army to garrison at Ganzhou and advanced
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixtieth year Yunti led his army to garrison at Ganzhou and advanced

sentences.zh: 次吐魯番。

translations.literal: next to Turpan.
translations.idiomatic: next to Turpan.

sentences.zh: 旋請於明年進兵。

translations.literal: He soon requested to advance the following year.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested permission to advance the following year.

sentences.zh: 閏六月，和爾博斯厄穆齊寨桑以厄魯特兵五百圍回民，回餘人乞援。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month, the zaisang of He'erbosi Emuqi used five hundred Oirat troops to besiege Muslims; the remaining Hui people begged for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month, the zaisang of He'erbosi Emuqi used five hundred Oirat troops to besiege Muslim communities; the surviving Hui people begged for relief.

sentences.zh: 允禵以糧運艱阻，兵難久駐，若徙入內地，亦苦糧少地狹，哈密扎薩克額敏皆不能容，布隆吉爾、達里圖諸地又阻瀚海，請諭靖逆將軍富寧安相機援撫，從之。

translations.literal: Yunti, because grain transport was difficult and troops could not remain long, and because moving into the interior would also suffer from scarce grain and narrow land while the Hami zaisak Emin could not accommodate them, and Bulongji'er, Dalitu, and other places were blocked by the desert sea, requested that Pacifying General Funing'an be instructed to give relief and pacification as circumstances allowed; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yunti argued that grain transport was arduous and troops could not remain long on campaign; even a withdrawal into the interior would mean too little grain and too little land, while the Hami zaisak Emin could not take them in, and Bulongji'er, Dalitu, and other places were cut off by the desert. He requested that Pacifying General Funing'an be instructed to give relief and pacification as circumstances allowed, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十月，召來京，面授方略。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was summoned to the capital and given strategy in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was summoned to the capital, where the Emperor personally instructed him in strategy.

sentences.zh: 六十一年三月，還軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixty-first year he returned with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixty-first year he returned with the army.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，諭總理王大臣曰：「西路軍務，大將軍職任重大，但於皇考大事若不來京，恐於心不安，速行文大將軍王馳驛來京。」

translations.literal: When the Shizong succeeded to the throne, he instructed the chief princes: "Western-route military affairs are weighty, and the Commander-in-Chief's duty is grave; yet if he does not come to the capital for our late father's great mourning, I fear my heart will not be at ease. Quickly send word to the Commander-in-Chief Prince to come posthaste to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor succeeded to the throne, he instructed the chief princes: "Western-route military affairs are weighty and the Commander-in-Chief's duty is grave; yet if he does not come to the capital for our late father's great mourning, I fear my heart will not be at ease. Send word at once to the Commander-in-Chief Prince to come posthaste to the capital."

sentences.zh: 允禵至，命留景陵待大祭。

translations.literal: When Yunti arrived, he was ordered to remain at Jingling to await the grand mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunti arrived, he was ordered to remain at Jingling to await the grand mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年五月，諭曰：「允禵無知狂悖，氣傲心高，​​朕望其改悔，以便加恩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongzheng an edict said: "Yunti is ignorant and arrogant, proud in spirit and lofty in heart. I hope he will repent so that favor may be shown him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongzheng 1 an edict said: "Yunti is ignorant and arrogant, proud in spirit and lofty in heart. I hope he will repent so that favor may yet be shown him.

sentences.zh: 今又恐其不能改，不及恩施，特進為郡王，慰我皇妣皇太后之心。」

translations.literal: Now I again fear he cannot reform, and before grace is extended, I specially promote him to junwang to comfort the heart of my empress dowager mother."
translations.idiomatic: Now I again fear he will not reform, and before grace can be extended I specially promote him to junwang to comfort the heart of my empress dowager mother."

sentences.zh: 三年三月，宗人府劾允禵前為大將軍，苦累兵丁，侵擾地方，糜費軍帑，請降授鎮國公，上命仍降貝子。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunti for, while Commander-in-Chief, overworking soldiers, harassing the region, and wasting military funds; it requested reduction to gengguo gong, but the Emperor ordered reduction only to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongzheng 3 the Imperial Clan Court impeached Yunti for, while serving as Commander-in-Chief, overworking the troops, harassing the region, and wasting military funds; it requested that he be reduced to gengguo gong, but the Emperor ordered that he be reduced only to beizi.

sentences.zh: 四年，諸王大臣劾，請正國法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the princes and great ministers impeached him and requested that the national law be applied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the princes and great ministers impeached him and requested that the full penalty of the law be applied.

sentences.zh: 諭：「允禵止於糊塗狂妄，其奸詐陰險與允禩、允禟相去甚遠。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Yunti is no more than muddle-headed and arrogant; in treachery, deceit, and secret malice he is far removed from Yinsi and Yuntang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Yunti is no more than muddle-headed and arrogant; in treachery, deceit, and secret malice he is far removed from Yinsi and Yuntang.

sentences.zh: 朕於諸人行事，知之甚悉，非獨於允禵有所偏徇。

translations.literal: I know the conduct of all these men very thoroughly and am not partial to Yunti alone.
translations.idiomatic: I know the conduct of all these men very thoroughly and am not showing partiality to Yunti alone.

sentences.zh: 今允禵居馬蘭峪，欲其瞻仰景陵，痛滌前非。

translations.literal: Now that Yunti dwells at Malanyu, it is my wish that he behold Jingling and thoroughly cleanse himself of past faults.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Yunti dwells at Malanyu, it is my wish that he behold Jingling and thoroughly cleanse himself of past faults.

sentences.zh: 允禵不能悔悟，奸民蔡懷璽又造為聽，宜加禁錮，即與其子白起並錮於壽皇殿左右，寬以歲月，待其改悔？

translations.literal: Yunti could not repent; the rogue Cai Huaibao also fabricated treasonous words to delude the people. He should be placed under confinement, and he and his son Bai Qi should be confined together on either side of the Shouhuang Hall, allowing time over the months and years for repentance."
translations.idiomatic: Yunti could not repent; the rogue Cai Huaibao also fabricated treasonous words to delude the people. He should be placed under confinement, and he and his son Bai Qi should be confined together on either side of the Shouhuang Hall, allowing time over the months and years for repentance."

sentences.zh: 大逆之言，搖惑」高宗即位，命釋之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he ordered Yunti released.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he ordered Yunti released.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，封輔國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he was enfeoffed as fuguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 he was enfeoffed as fuguo gong.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twelfth year he was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，進封恂郡王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was promoted and enfeoffed as Prince Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was promoted and enfeoffed as Prince Xun.

sentences.zh: 二十年六月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twentieth year he died; a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twentieth year he died and was given the posthumous title Qin.

sentences.zh: 第一子弘春，雍正元年，封貝子。

translations.literal: His first son Hongchun, in the first year of Yongzheng, was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: His first son Hongchun was enfeoffed as beizi in Yongzheng 1.

sentences.zh: 二年，坐允禩黨，革爵。

translations.literal: In the second year he was convicted as a member of Yinsi's faction and stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was convicted as a member of Yinsi's faction and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 四年，封鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as gengguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as gengguo gong.

sentences.zh: 六年，進貝子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to beizi.

sentences.zh: 九年，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 十一年，封泰郡王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince Tai.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，諭責弘春輕佻，复降貝子。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year an edict rebuked Hongchun for frivolity, and he was again reduced to beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year an edict rebuked Hongchun for frivolity, and he was again reduced to beizi.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，奪爵。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor succeeded to the throne, his title was stripped.

sentences.zh: 別封允禵第二子弘明為貝勒。

translations.literal: Yunti's second son Hongming was separately enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: Yunti's second son Hongming was separately enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十二年，卒，諡恭勤。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Qianlong he died; posthumous title Gongqin was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Qianlong he died and was given the posthumous title Gongqin.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以不入八分鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were demoted by successive degrees according to precedent, with hereditary succession at the rank of buru bafen gengguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants were demoted by successive degrees according to precedent, and the line continued at the rank of buru bafen gengguo gong.

sentences.zh: 弘春曾孫奕山，自有傳。

translations.literal: Hongchun's great-grandson Yishan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Hongchun's great-grandson Yishan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 愉恪郡王允潖，聖祖第十五子。

translations.literal: Prince Yu the Ke Yinpiao was the Kangxi Emperor's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu the Ke, Yinpiao, was the fifteenth son of the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年，從幸塞外。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi he accompanied the Emperor on a tour beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi he accompanied the Emperor on a tour beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 自是輒從。

translations.literal: From then on he always followed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always accompanied the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，封貝勒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was enfeoffed as beile.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 he was enfeoffed as beile.

sentences.zh: 命守景陵。

translations.literal: He was ordered to guard Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to guard Jingling.

sentences.zh: 八年，封愉郡王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Prince Yu.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year he died; a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year he died and was given a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子弘慶，襲。

translations.literal: His son Hongqing succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongqing succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十四年，薨，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong he died; posthumous title Gong was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong he died and was given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子永珔，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yongbing succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongbing succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were demoted by successive degrees according to precedent, with hereditary succession at the rank of fuguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants were demoted by successive degrees according to precedent, and the line continued at the rank of fuguo gong.

sentences.zh: 果毅親王允禮，聖祖第十七子。

translations.literal: Prince Guo the Resolute Yunli was the Kangxi Emperor's seventeenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guo the Resolute, Yunli, was the seventeenth son of the Kangxi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十四年，從幸塞外。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Kangxi he accompanied the Emperor on a tour beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year of Kangxi he accompanied the Emperor on a tour beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 自是輒從。

translations.literal: From then on he always followed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always accompanied the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，封果郡王，管理藩院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was enfeoffed as Prince Guo and put in charge of Lifan Yuan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was enfeoffed as Prince Guo and put in charge of Lifan Yuan affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，諭曰：「果郡王實心為國，操守清廉，宜給親王俸，護衞亦如之，班在順承郡王上。」

translations.literal: In the third year an edict said: "Prince Guo serves the state with a sincere heart and maintains incorrupt conduct; he should be granted a qinwang stipend, with guards likewise, and rank above the Prince of Shuncheng."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict said: "Prince Guo serves the state with a sincere heart and maintains incorrupt conduct; he should be granted a qinwang stipend, with guards likewise, and rank above the Prince of Shuncheng."

sentences.zh: 六年，進親王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to qinwang.

sentences.zh: 七年，命管工部事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to manage Board of Works affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered to manage Board of Works affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年，命總理戶部三庫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to supervise the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was ordered to supervise the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授宗令，管戶部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed clan commander and put in charge of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed clan commander and put in charge of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十二年，命赴泰寧，送達賴喇嘛還西藏，循途巡閱諸省駐防及綠營兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered to go to Taining to escort the Dalai Lama back to Tibet, and en route to inspect garrison troops and Green Standard forces in the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was ordered to go to Taining to escort the Dalai Lama back to Tibet, and en route to inspect garrison troops and Green Standard forces in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 十三年，還京師，命辦理苗疆事務。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he returned to the capital and was ordered to handle Miao frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he returned to the capital and was ordered to handle Miao frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 世宗疾大漸，受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: When the Shizong's illness grew critical, he received the testamentary edict to serve as regent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongzheng Emperor's illness grew critical, he received the testamentary edict to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命總理事務，解宗令，管刑部。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he was ordered to manage affairs generally, relieved as clan commander, and put in charge of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was ordered to manage affairs generally, relieved as clan commander, and put in charge of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋賜親王雙俸，免宴見叩拜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted a double qinwang stipend and exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted a double qinwang stipend and exempted from bowing at banquets and audiences.

sentences.zh: 密疏請蠲江南諸省民欠漕項、蘆課、學租、雜稅，允之。

translations.literal: In a secret memorial he requested remission of the people's arrears in grain transport dues, reed levies, school rents, and miscellaneous taxes in the Jiangnan provinces; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In a secret memorial he requested remission of the people's arrears in grain transport dues, reed levies, school rents, and miscellaneous taxes in the Jiangnan provinces, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「果親王秉性忠直，皇考所信任。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Prince Guo is loyal and upright by nature and was trusted by my late father.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Prince Guo is loyal and upright by nature and was trusted by my late father.

sentences.zh: 外間頗疑其嚴厲，今觀密奏，足見其存心寬厚，特以宣示九卿。」

translations.literal: Outside the court many suspected him of severity; now, reading this secret memorial, one can see how generous his heart truly is. I specially display it to the Nine Ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Outside the court many suspected him of severity; now, reading this secret memorial, one can see how generous his heart truly is. I specially display it to the Nine Ministers."

sentences.zh: 允禮體弱，上命在邸治事，越數日一入直。

translations.literal: Yunli was weak in body; the Emperor ordered him to manage affairs from his residence, entering duty only once every several days.
translations.idiomatic: Yunli was weak in body; the Emperor ordered him to manage affairs from his residence, entering duty only once every several days.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，坐事，罷雙俸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was convicted of an offense and his double stipend was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1 he was convicted of an offense and his double stipend was revoked.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，病篤，遣和親王弘晝往視。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, when his illness grew critical, Prince He Hongzhou was dispatched to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, when his illness grew critical, Prince He Hongzhou was dispatched to visit him.

sentences.zh: 二月，薨，上震悼，即日親臨其喪。

translations.literal: In the second month he died; the Emperor was deeply grieved and personally attended the funeral that same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he died; the Emperor was deeply grieved and personally attended the funeral that same day.

sentences.zh: 予諡。

translations.literal: A posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 無子，莊親王允祿等請以世宗第六子弘曕爲之後。

translations.literal: He had no sons; Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others requested that the Shizong's sixth son Hongyan be made his successor.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; Prince Zhuang Yunlu and others requested that the Yongzheng Emperor's sixth son Hongyan be made his successor.

sentences.zh: 弘適善詩詞，雅好藏書，與怡府明善堂埒。

translations.literal: Hongyan was skilled in poetry and song and dearly loved collecting books, rivaling the Mingshan Hall of the Prince of Yi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyan was skilled in poetry and dearly loved collecting books, rivaling the Mingshan Hall library of the Prince of Yi's household.

sentences.zh: 禦下嚴，晨起披衣巡視，遇不法者立杖之，故無敢為非者。

translations.literal: He was strict with subordinates; rising in the morning he would put on his robe and make the rounds, and on encountering lawless conduct would immediately have the offender beaten, so none dared do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He was strict with subordinates; each morning he would rise, put on his robe, and make the rounds, and on encountering lawless conduct would immediately have the offender beaten, so none dared do wrong.

sentences.zh: 節儉善居積，嘗以開煤？

translations.literal: Frugal and skilled at accumulating wealth, he once, by opening coal mines,
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and skilled at accumulating wealth, he once opened coal mines

sentences.zh: 奪民產。

translations.literal: seized people's property.
translations.idiomatic: and seized people's property.

sentences.zh: 從上南巡，囑兩淮鹽政高恒鬻人葠牟利，又令織造關差致繡段、玩器，予賤值。

translations.literal: Accompanying the Emperor on the southern tour, he instructed the Liang-Huai salt commissioner Gao Heng to sell ginseng for profit, and also ordered the imperial weaving commission agents to deliver brocades and curios, paying paltry prices.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern tour he instructed the Liang-Huai salt commissioner Gao Heng to sell ginseng for profit, and ordered imperial weaving agents to deliver brocades and curios at cut-rate prices.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，圓明園九州清宴災，弘適後至，與諸皇子談笑露齒，上不懌。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, fire struck the Jiuzhou Qingyan at Yuanming Yuan; Hongshi arrived late and, with the other princes, laughed and talked with teeth showing; the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, when fire destroyed the Jiuzhou Qingyan at the Old Summer Palace, Hongshi arrived late and laughed openly with the other princes; the Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又嘗以門下私人囑阿里袞。

translations.literal: He also once entrusted a private follower from his household to Arigun.
translations.idiomatic: He also once asked Arigun to take on a private follower from his household.

sentences.zh: 上發其罪，並責其奉母妃儉薄，降貝勒，罷一切差使。

translations.literal: The Emperor exposed his crimes and also rebuked him for treating his mother the consort parsimoniously; he was demoted to beile and stripped of all appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor exposed his crimes and rebuked him for treating his mother the consort with undue frugality; he was demoted to beile and stripped of every appointment.

sentences.zh: 自是家居閉門，意抑鬱不自聊。

translations.literal: From then on he remained at home behind closed doors, dejected and ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he shut himself up at home, depressed and unable to find peace.

sentences.zh: 三十年三月，病篤，上往撫視。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirtieth year, when his illness grew critical, the Emperor went to visit and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirtieth year, when his illness turned grave, the Emperor went to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 弘適於臥榻間叩首引咎，上執其手，痛曰：「以汝年少，故稍加拂拭，何愧恧若此？」

translations.literal: On his sickbed Hongshi kowtowed and took blame upon himself; the Emperor took his hand and said in anguish: "Because you are still young, I merely sought to brush you up a little—why such shame and remorse?"
translations.idiomatic: On his sickbed Hongshi kowtowed and accepted blame; the Emperor took his hand and said in anguish, "You are still young—I only meant to polish you a little. Why such shame and remorse?"

sentences.zh: 因復封郡王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again enfeoffed as junwang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reinstated as a prince of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 旋薨，予諡。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, and was given a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 子永瑹，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yongshu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongshu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，薨，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he died; posthumous title Jian was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he died and was posthumously titled Jian.

sentences.zh: 子綿從，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Miancong succeeded as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Miancong succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 孫奕湘，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: His grandson Yixiang succeeded as gengguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yixiang succeeded as Prince of the Fourth Rank.

sentences.zh: 歷官副都統，廣州、盛京將軍，兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He held the posts of vice commander-in-chief, commander at Guangzhou and Shengjing, and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commander-in-chief, as commander at Guangzhou and Mukden, and as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 加貝子銜。

translations.literal: The rank of beizi was added to his title.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the rank of beizi in addition to his title.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恪慎。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Keqen was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Keqen.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以輔國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were demoted by successive degrees, with hereditary succession at the rank of fuguo gong.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants were demoted by successive degrees, with the title passing hereditarily at the rank of fuguo gong.

sentences.zh: 簡靖貝勒允禕，聖祖第二十子，

translations.literal: Beile Yunyi, posthumously Prince Jian the Tranquil, was the Kangxi Emperor's twentieth son,
translations.idiomatic: Beile Yunyi, posthumously Prince Jian the Tranquil, was the Kangxi Emperor's twentieth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十五年，始從幸塞外，自是輒從。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Kangxi, he first accompanied the Emperor on tours beyond the passes; from then on he always followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year of Kangxi, in Kangxi 55 he first accompanied the Emperor beyond the passes, and from then on always did so.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，封貝子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was enfeoffed as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 he was enfeoffed as beizi.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，進貝勒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year he was promoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eighth year he was promoted to beile.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，命祭陵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to perform tomb sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to perform sacrifices at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 稱病不行，降輔國公。

translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-ninth year and was given the posthumous title Jin.

sentences.zh: 弟綿循，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Mianxun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mianxun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing he died; posthumous title Ke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing and was given the posthumous title Ke.

sentences.zh: 子奕亨，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His son Yiheng inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiheng succeeded as beile.

sentences.zh: 卒，子載容，襲貝子。

translations.literal: He died; his son Zairong inherited as beizi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; his son Zairong succeeded as beizi.

sentences.zh: 同治中，加貝勒銜。

translations.literal: During the Tongzhi reign he was granted the rank of beile.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi reign he was granted beile rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡敏恪。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Minke was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Minke.

sentences.zh: 子溥廉，襲鎮國公。

translations.literal: His son Pulian inherited as Defender of the State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pulian succeeded as Defender of the State.

sentences.zh: 懷親王福惠，世宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai Fuhui was the Shizong's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fuhui, Huai, was the Yongzheng Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 八歲殤。

translations.literal: He died young at eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at the age of eight.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，追封親王，諡曰​​懷。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as qinwang with posthumous title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong succeeded to the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince of the first rank with the posthumous title Huai.
